title: Charges on Benefits and Recovery of Excess Payments.
heading: 9.07 Charges on Benefits and Recovery of Excess Payments.
start_phrase: All benefits in respect of a Member under the Plan shall stand char ged with and be subject to deductions therefrom of all sums in respect of losses to a member of the PepsiCo Or ganization or Employer or otherwise caused by misdemeanor of the Member and on production by the member of the PepsiCo Or ganization or Employer of proof satisfactory to the V ice President that any such loss ought to be made good by a Member .
summary:
- Section 9.07 (Charges on Benefits and Recovery of Excess Payments):
  - Plan benefits may be reduced to reimburse the Employer or PepsiCo Organization for losses caused by a Member’s misconduct, upon proof satisfactory to the Vice President; deducted amounts are paid to the affected employer entity as a full discharge.
  - Any overpayment, premature, or misdirected payment (“Excess Payment”) must be returned to the Plan.
  - To recover Excess Payments (with interest), the Plan has nonexclusive rights including:
    - A constructive trust and first-priority equitable lien on the Excess Payment, its proceeds, or substitutes, enforceable even after transfers.
    - The right, at the Vice President’s discretion, to offset other amounts otherwise payable to the recipient.
    - The right to pursue legal or equitable actions in any competent court; recipients submit to such jurisdictions and waive related defenses.
  - Recipients must cooperate and take actions requested by the Vice President to facilitate recovery. These provisions maximize and do not limit the Plan’s recovery rights.

- Section 9.08 (Prohibited Misconduct) [partial]:
  - If the Vice President determines a Member engaged in Prohibited Misconduct at any time up to the second anniversary of termination, the Member forfeits all Pay Credits and Interest Credits (past, current, and future), and the Member’s PIRP-DC Account is adjusted to reflect the forfeiture.
text:
07    Charges on Benefits and Recovery of Excess Payments.
All benefits in respect of a Member under the Plan shall stand char ged with and be subject to deductions therefrom of all
sums in respect of losses to a member of the PepsiCo Or ganization or Employer or otherwise caused by misdemeanor of the
Member and on production by the member of the PepsiCo Or ganization or Employer of proof satisfactory to the V ice President
that any such loss ought to be made good by a Member . The relevant amount shall be deductible from the Member ’s benefits and
be payable to the Employer or member of the PepsiCo Or ganization whose receipt shall be a valid dischar ge for the same.
Payments to, for or in connection with a Member that are made (as of a point in time and to any person or entity) may not
exceed the exact amount of payments that are due as of such time and to such person, as provided by the terms of the Plan that
specify the amounts that are payable, the time as of which they are payable, and the person to whom they are payable.
Accordingly , any such excess payment or any other overpayment, premature payment or misdirected payment (one or more of
which are hereafter referred to as an “Excess Payment”) may not be retained by the party receiving it, but must be restored
promptly to the Plan. In exchange for Member or beneficiary status hereunder (or for having any other direct or indirect right or
claim of right from the Plan, or solely as a result of having received an Excess Payment), any party receiving an Excess Payment
grants to the Plan the following nonexclusive rights –
(1)    A constructive trust and first priority equitable lien on any payment that is received directly or
indirectly from the Plan and that is, in whole or part, an Excess Payment (such trust and lien shall be equal to the
amount of the Excess Payment increased by appropriate interest) or upon the proceeds or substitutes for such
payment, and any transfer shall be subject to such constructive trust and equitable lien (including a transfer to a
person, trust fund or entity).
(2)    The right to of fset (as necessary to recover the Excess Payment with appropriate interest)
other payments that are properly payable by the Plan to the recipient of the Excess Payment; however , reliance on
this right is in the discretion of the V ice President, and the existence of an opportunity to apply it shall not
diminish the Plan’ s rights under paragraph (1) above.
(3)    The right to bring any equitable or legal action or proceeding with respect to the enforcement
of any rights in this Section in any court of competent jurisdiction as the Plan may elect, and following receipt of
an Excess Payment the Member hereby submits to each such jurisdiction, waiving any and all rights that may
correspond to such party’ s present or future residence.
Any party receiving an Excess Payment shall promptly take all actions requested by the V ice President that are in
furtherance of the Plan’ s recovery of the Excess Payment with appropriate interest. In all cases, this subsection shall
maximize the rights of the Plan to recover improper payments and shall not restrict the rights of the Plan in any way ,
including with respect to any improper payment that is not addressed above.
9.

title: Prohibited Misconduct.
heading: 9.08 Pr ohibited Misconduct.
start_phrase: (a) Notwithstanding any other provision of this Plan to the contrary , if the V ice President determines that a Member has engaged in Prohibited Misconduct at any time prior to the second anniversary of his termination of employment with the PepsiCo Or ganization, the Member shall forfeit all Pay Credits and Interest Credits (whether paid previously , being paid currently or payable in the future), and his PIRP-DC Account shall be adjusted to reflect such forfeiture and previously paid Pay Credits and Interest Credits shall be recovered.
summary:
- Charges on benefits and recovery of excess payments (Section 9.07):
  - Member benefits can be reduced to cover losses to PepsiCo or the Employer caused by the Member’s misdemeanor, upon proof satisfactory to the Vice President.
  - Any overpayment, premature, or misdirected payment (“Excess Payment”) must be returned to the Plan.
  - The Plan has a constructive trust and first-priority equitable lien (with interest) over Excess Payments and their proceeds.
  - The Plan may offset future amounts payable to the recipient to recover Excess Payments, at the Vice President’s discretion.
  - The Plan may pursue legal or equitable actions in any chosen jurisdiction; recipients submit to such jurisdiction.
  - Recipients must cooperate to restore Excess Payments with interest; the subsection maximizes the Plan’s recovery rights.

- Prohibited Misconduct and forfeiture (Section 9.08):
  - If the Vice President determines a Member engaged in Prohibited Misconduct at any time up to two years after termination, the Member forfeits all Pay Credits and Interest Credits (past, current, or future), and previously paid amounts will be recovered; Members agree to repay.
  - Prohibited Misconduct includes:
    - Participating (broadly defined) in businesses that market/sell/distribute/produce “Covered Products” (with a narrow non-competing retail/consumption exception).
    - Soliciting PepsiCo employees to leave or join other entities.
    - Using or disclosing PepsiCo confidential information outside job needs.
    - Acts contrary to PepsiCo’s interests (e.g., Code of Conduct violations, insider trading, gross misconduct).
    - Fraud.
  - Whistleblower protection: Members may communicate with government authorities, participate in investigations, and receive awards; attorney‑client privilege is preserved. DTSA safe harbor permits certain confidential or sealed disclosures of trade secrets, including in retaliation lawsuits under specified conditions.
  - Definitions:
    - “Participation” includes serving, advising, consulting, or endorsing competing entities/products.
    - “Covered Products” broadly include beverages (e.g., soft drinks, tea, water, juices, sports/energy/coffee/dairy drinks), juices/juice products, dairy, snacks (salty/sweet/meat/granola/cereal bars/cookies), hot cereals, pancake mixes/syrups, value‑added rice/pasta, ready‑to‑eat cereals, dry pasta, and products/services under development known to the Member.

- Notices (Section 9.09):
  - Notices to the Plan are sufficient if in writing and delivered to the Vice President.
  - Notices to Members may be sent to the last known address or via other reasonably available methods (e.g., electronic) as determined by the Vice President.

- Plan documentation (Section 9.10):
  - Members are entitled to a copy of the Plan upon request.

- Currency of payment (Section 9.11):
  - Benefits are paid in U.S. dollars or another eligible currency approved by the Vice President.
  - Currency conversion follows a methodology approved by the Vice President.
text:
08    Pr ohibited Misconduct.
(a) Notwithstanding any other provision of this Plan to the contrary , if the V ice President determines that a
Member has engaged in Prohibited Misconduct at any time prior to the second anniversary of his termination of
employment with the PepsiCo Or ganization, the Member shall forfeit all Pay Credits and Interest Credits (whether paid
previously , being paid currently or payable in the future), and his PIRP-DC Account shall be adjusted to reflect such
forfeiture and previously paid Pay Credits and Interest Credits
20shall be recovered. As a condition to Membership in this Plan, each Member agrees to this and each Member agrees to
repay PepsiCo the amounts it seeks to recover under this Section 9.08.
(b) Any of the following activities engaged in, directly or indirectly , by a Member shall constitute Prohibited
Misconduct:
(1) The Member accepting any employment, assignment, position or responsibility , or acquiring any
ownership interest, which involves the Member ’s “Participation” (as defined below) in a business entity that
markets, sells, distributes or produces “Covered Products” (as defined below), unless such business entity makes
retail sales or consumes Covered Products without in any way competing with the PepsiCo Or ganization.
(2) The Member , directly or indirectly (including through someone else acting on the Member ’s
recommendation, suggestion, identification or advice), soliciting any PepsiCo Or ganization employee to leave the
PepsiCo Or ganization’ s employment or to accept any position with any other entity .
(3) The Member using or disclosing to anyone any confidential information regarding the PepsiCo
Organization other than as necessary in his position with the PepsiCo Or ganization. Such confidential information
shall include all non-public information the Member acquired as a result of his positions with the PepsiCo
Organization. Examples of such confidential information include non-public information about the PepsiCo
Organization’ s customers, suppliers, distributors and potential acquisition tar gets; its business operations and
structure; its product lines, formulas and pricing; its processes, machines and inventions; its research and know-
how; its financial data; and its plans and strategies.
(4) The Member engaging in any acts that are considered to be contrary to the PepsiCo Or ganization’ s best
interests, including violating the Corporation’ s Code of Conduct, engaging in unlawful trading in the securities of
the Corporation or of any other company based on information gained as a result of his employment with the
PepsiCo Or ganization, or engaging in any other activity which constitutes gross misconduct.
(5) The Member engaging in any activity that constitutes fraud.
21Notwithstanding the foregoing and for the avoidance of doubt, nothing in this Plan shall prohibit the Member from
communicating with government authorities concerning any possible legal violations without notice to the Corporation,
participating in government investigations, and/or receiving any applicable award for providing information to
government authorities. The Corporation nonetheless asserts and does not waive its attorney-client privilege over any
information appropriately protected by the privilege. Further , pursuant to the Defend T rade Secrets Act, an individual
shall not be held criminally or civilly liable under any federal or state trade secret law for the disclosure of a trade secret
that (A) is made (i) in confidence to a federal, state, or local government of ficial, either directly or indirectly , or to an
attorney; and (ii) solely for the purpose of reporting or investigating a suspected violation of law; or (B) is made in a
complaint or other document filed in a lawsuit or other proceeding, if such filing is made under seal. An individual who
files a lawsuit for retaliation by an employer for reporting a suspected violation of law may disclose the trade secret to the
attorney of the individual and use the trade secret information in the court proceeding, if the individual (A) files any
document containing the trade secret under seal; and (B) does not disclose the trade secret, except pursuant to court order .
For purposes of this subsection, “Participation” shall be construed broadly to include: (i) serving as a director , officer,
employee, consultant or contractor with respect to such a business entity; (ii) providing input, advice, guidance or
suggestions to such a business entity; or (iii) providing a recommendation or testimonial on behalf of such a business
entity or one or more products it produces. For purposes of this subsection, “Covered Products” shall mean any product
that falls into one or more of the following categories, so long as the PepsiCo Or ganization is producing, marketing,
selling or licensing such product anywhere in the world – beverages, including without limitation carbonated soft drinks,
tea, water , juice drinks, sports drinks, cof fee drinks, ener gy drinks, and value-added dairy drinks; juices and juice
products; dairy products; snacks, including salty snacks, sweet snacks meat snacks, granola and cereal bars, and cookies;
hot cereals; pancake mixes; value-added rice products; pancake syrups; value-added pasta products; ready-to-eat cereals;
dry pasta products; or any product or service that the Member had reason to know was under development by the PepsiCo
Organization during the Member ’s employment with the PepsiCo Or ganization.

Benefit Enhancements are determined after year-end once non-U.S. Person status is confirmed; in a benefit commencement year, the Vice President may authorize an enhancement if satisfied the member will not be a U.S. Person, otherwise benefits start without enhancement and may be adjusted the following year. title: Exemption from ERISA.
heading: 9.13 Exemption fr om ERISA.
start_phrase: The Plan is intended to be exempt from the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended (“ERISA”), as a plan maintained outside of the United States primarily for the benefit of persons substantially all of whom are nonresident aliens of the United States.
summary:
- Governing Law: The plan is governed by and interpreted under New York law and applicable federal law as applied by U.S. District Courts in New York.
- ERISA Exemption: The plan is intended to be exempt from ERISA as a non-U.S. plan primarily for nonresident aliens. Active membership is limited to nonresident aliens working outside the U.S., and permanent records are to be maintained outside the U.S.
- Section 409A Exemption: The plan is designed to remain completely exempt from IRC Section 409A. No U.S. Person may receive any “Benefit Enhancement” (vesting, increase, or enhancement) based on compensation or service while a U.S. Person. Interest Credits may apply only to amounts derived from non-U.S.-person service. Benefit Enhancements are determined after year-end upon confirming non-U.S.-person status, with limited authority for the Vice President to allow an enhancement in the commencement year if non-U.S.-person status is confirmed; otherwise, benefits start without the enhancement and may be adjusted the following year. The Vice President has overriding authority to ensure Section 409A exemption, superseding any conflicting plan provisions.
- Electronic Signatures: Electronic signatures and electronic records by relevant parties (including the Vice President, Eligible Employees, and Dependents) have the same legal effect as manual signatures and paper records, to the fullest extent permitted by law.

13    Exemption fr om ERISA.
The Plan is intended to be exempt from the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended (“ERISA”),
as a plan maintained outside of the United States primarily for the benefit of persons substantially all of whom are nonresident
aliens of the United States. In order to preserve this exemption from ERISA, Active Membership in the Plan shall be limited to
individuals who are nonresident aliens of the United States and whose assigned work locations are outside the United States, and
it is intended that all permanent records and documentation relating to the administration of the Plan shall be kept at a location
that is outside of the United States.

title: Exemption from Section 409A.
heading: 9.14 Exemption fr om Section 409A.
start_phrase: In order to permit this Plan to be completely exempt from United States Internal Revenue Code section 409A (“Section 409A”), this Plan shall be subject to the special operating rules and limitations in this Section 9.14, ef fective for any period to which Section 409A applies.
summary:
- Governing Law: The Plan is governed by New York law and applicable federal law as applied by U.S. District Courts in New York.
- ERISA Exemption: The Plan is intended to be exempt from ERISA as an offshore plan for nonresident aliens; Active Membership is limited to nonresident aliens with assigned work locations outside the U.S., and permanent administrative records are to be maintained outside the U.S.
- Section 409A Exemption: The Plan is designed to be fully exempt from IRC Section 409A with special rules:
  - No Benefit Enhancements (vesting/increases) based on compensation or service while a Member is a U.S. Person.
  - Interest Credits may be granted to U.S. Persons only on PIRP-DC balances derived from Pay Credits for non-U.S. service (and related Interest Credits).
  - Benefit Enhancements for a year are determined only after confirming post-year-end that the Member was not a U.S. Person for that year.
  - In the benefit commencement year, the Vice President may authorize a Benefit Enhancement if satisfied the Member will not be a U.S. Person; otherwise benefits start without that year’s enhancement, with adjustments the following year if warranted.
  - The Section 409A exemption requirement overrides any conflicting Plan provisions, and the Vice President has broad authority to ensure compliance.
- Electronic Signatures: Electronic signatures and electronic recordkeeping are permitted and have the same legal effect as manual signatures and paper records, to the fullest extent allowed by law.
text:
14    Exemption fr om Section 409A.
In order to permit this Plan to be completely exempt from United States Internal Revenue Code section 409A (“Section
409A”), this Plan shall be subject to the special operating rules and limitations in this Section 9.14, ef fective for any period to
which Section 409A applies. It is the intent of the Plan that no Member who is a U.S. Person may in any way have their benefit
from the Plan vest, increase or in any way be enhanced (collectively , a “Benefit Enhancement”) as a result of their compensation
or service while a U.S. Person. However , Interest Credits may be provided on the PIRP-DC Account of a Member who is a U.S.
Person, but only to the extent the balance in the PIRP-DC Account is derived from Pay Credits that relate to Service completed
while the Member was not a U.S. Person (and Interest Credits on such Pay Credits). Accordingly , no Member shall become
entitled to a Benefit Enhancement with respect to a calendar year until it is determined, following the close of such year , that the
Member was not a U.S. Person with respect to such year . Notwithstanding the preceding sentence, in the calendar year a
Member ’s benefit under this Plan is scheduled to commence, the V ice President may authorize a Benefit Enhancement for the
calendar year of benefit commencement to the extent the V ice President determines satisfactorily that the Member will not be a
U.S. Person for such year . In other cases, the Member ’s benefit will commence under this Plan without any Benefit Enhancement
related to the calendar year of commencement, and appropriate adjustments will be made to the Member ’s benefit in the
following year if it is determined that the Member was not a U.S. Person in such calendar year of commencement. This Section
9.14 shall at all times be interpreted and applied in accordance with the overriding requirement that allocations, benefits and
rights under the Plan must remain entirely exempt from Section 409A, and the V ice President shall have such unrestricted
authority as is necessary to ensure that it is applied in accordance with this requirement. Further , to ensure the continuation of
such exemption from Section 409A, the preceding sentence shall be applied and given overriding ef fect notwithstanding any
other provision or language in this Plan.

title: Foreword
heading:
ARTICLE I
Foreword
start_phrase:
The PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (“PEP” or “Plan”) has been established by PepsiCo for the
benefit of salaried employees of the PepsiCo Organization who participate in the Salaried Plan.
summary:
- Purpose and scope: The PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (PEP) provides supplemental pension benefits to salaried employees who participate in the Salaried Plan, making up benefits limited by the Internal Revenue Code and, for certain employees, providing benefits based on the pre-1989 Salaried Plan formula.

- Historical restatements: The Plan was restated in 1989 and again effective January 1, 2005 to establish the Section 409A Program covering benefits earned/vested after December 31, 2004 or materially modified thereafter.

- Merger with PBG PEP: Effective December 31, 2011, the PBG Pension Equalization Plan merged into PEP. The 409A PBG PEP Document (as of April 1, 2009, amended through January 1, 2011) remains applicable to pre-merger 409A-governed benefits, with certain administrative provisions now governed by the main 409A PepsiCo PEP document. The merger and document updates did not change the time or form of payment for 409A benefits.

- Subsequent restatements: The 409A Program Document was restated effective January 1 of 2017, 2019, 2021, and most recently 2022.

- Interplay of 409A and Pre-409A Programs: Benefits not subject to Section 409A (generally earned/vested before January 1, 2005 and not materially modified) are governed by a separate Pre-409A Program document. Together they form a single plan, but amounts are tracked separately to preserve grandfathered status and exemption from Section 409A.

- Alignment with Salaried Plan freeze: Because PEP generally makes up benefits limited under the Salaried Plan, accruals and eligibility to “grow into” enhancements are tied to the Salaried Plan. The Salaried Plan freeze effective end of day December 31, 2025 also freezes all PEP accruals at that time. Post-2025 growth into enhancements under PEP follows the Salaried Plan’s operational rules. Certain participants may have additional accrual opportunities via the PEP Guarantee (Section 5.2) or Appendix provisions.

- Definitions and construction (Article II): Introduces defined terms and interpretation rules. Examples:
  - Accrued Benefit: Pension payable at Normal Retirement Date based on Highest Average Monthly Earnings and Credited Service.
  - Actuarial Equivalent: Benefits of equal value determined using specified actuarial factors applied uniformly; annuity and inflation-protection factors are selected by the Plan Administrator and, effective January 1, 2009, are set forth in Schedule 1 (with prior factors in the Appendix). New rights/features do not automatically adopt these factors unless expressly provided.

ARTICLE I
Foreword
The PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (“PEP” or “Plan”) has been established by PepsiCo for the
benefit of salaried employees of the PepsiCo Organization who participate in the Salaried Plan. PEP provides
benefits for eligible employees whose pension benefits under the Salaried Plan are limited by the provisions of the
Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended. In addition, PEP provides benefits for certain eligible employees based
on the pre-1989 Salaried Plan formula (see, for example, Part B thereof).
1989 Restatement . The Plan was amended and restated in its entirety in 1989.
409A Program Document 2005 Restatement . The Plan was last amended and restated in its entirety
effective as of January 1, 2005. The 2005 restatement sets forth the terms of the Plan that are applicable to benefits
that are subject to Section 409A, i.e., generally , benefits that are earned or vested after December 31, 2004 or
materially modified within the meaning of T reas. Reg. § 1.409A-6(a)(4) (the “409A Program”).
Amendments to the 2005 Restatement . The 2005 restatement was amended to reflect the merger into
this Plan of the PBG Pension Equalization Plan (“PBG PEP”), ef fective at the end of the day on December 31, 2011.
The PBG PEP document that was in ef fect on April 1, 2009, as amended through January 1, 2011 (the “409A PBG
PEP Document”) is attached hereto as Appendix Article PBG 409A and shall continue to govern PBG PEP benefits
that were subject to the 409A PBG PEP Document prior to the Plan merger , except for certain administrative
provisions that are now governed by the main portion of the 409A PepsiCo PEP Document as is explained in
Appendix Article PBG 409A. There has been no change to the time or form of payment of benefits that are subject to
Internal Revenue Code Section 409A (“Section 409A”)
- 1 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Programunder either the PepsiCo PEP or PBG PEP Documents as a result of the merger or the revisions to the 409A
PepsiCo PEP Document and 409A PBG PEP Document.
2017, 2019, 2021 and 2022 Restatements . This restatement of the 409A Program Document is
effective as of January 1, 2022. Before this restatement, the 409A Program Document was most recently restated
effective as of January 1, 2021, and prior to that, ef fective as of January 1, 2019, and prior to that, ef fective as of
January 1, 2017.
Interplay of this 409A Program and Pre-409A Program . All benefits under the Plan that are not subject
to the 409A Program (i.e., generally , benefits that are earned or vested before January 1, 2005 and not materially
modified thereafter within the meaning of T reas. Reg. § 1.409A-6(a)(4)) shall be governed by the Plan Document for
the Pre-Section 409 Program (the “Pre-409A Program”). Together , this document and the document for the Pre-409A
Program describe the terms of a single plan. However , amounts subject to the terms of this 409A Program and
amounts subject to the terms of the Pre-409A Program shall be tracked separately at all times. The preservation of
the terms of the Pre-409A Program, without material modification, and the separation between the 409A Program
amounts and the Pre-409A Program amounts are intended to be suf ficient to permit the pre-409A Program to remain
exempt from Section 409A as grandfathered benefits.
Freeze of the Salaried Plan . In general, the Plan provides benefits that make up for benefits that would
accrue under the Salaried Plan but for certain Code limitations on benefits and compensation that apply to the
Salaried Plan. As a result, a Participant’ s accrual of Plan benefits and a Participant’ s growing into certain benefit
enhancements (such as more favorable early commencement factors) are generally tied to the Participant’ s accrual
of benefits and growing into benefit enhancements under the Salaried Plan. For certain
- 2 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A ProgramParticipants, there are special provisions in Section 5.2 (the “PEP Guarantee”) or the Appendix that provide a benefit
accrual opportunity that goes beyond providing a make up for the application of certain Code limitations to the
Salaried Plan. Regardless, however , the freeze on accruals under the Salaried Plan that is ef fective as of the end of
the day on December 31, 2025 also freezes all accruals under this Plan ef fective as of that time. In addition, the
Salaried Plan’ s operational rules with respect to the ability to grow into benefit enhancements after December 31,
2025 govern the ability to grow into benefit enhancements after December 31, 2025 under this Plan.

summary:
- Article II sets out defined terms and interpretation rules for the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program, establishing how capitalized terms are used across the Plan and cross-referencing the Salaried Plan where applicable.
- Actuarial Equivalent rules:
  - Plan Administrator discretion to set and amend actuarial factors for all forms of payment (annuities and lump sums), applied uniformly and potentially retroactively to accrued benefits.
  - Schedule 1 specifies mortality tables and interest rates: GAR 94/5% for 1/1/2009–12/31/2018; from 1/1/2019, Salaried Plan’s 2019 mortality table with 5% (most forms), 4.2% (5% inflation protection), 4.6% (7% inflation protection).
  - “Not-less-than” protection aligns with 2019 Salaried Plan Factors for annuity starting dates on/after 1/1/2019.
  - Lump-sum equivalents use the Salaried Plan’s current lump-sum factors (excluding transition factors); other adjustments follow Salaried Plan factors.
- Core benefit forms and timing:
  - Definitions for Pension (distinguishing 409A vs Pre-409A portions), Annuity, Single Life Annuity, Qualified Joint & Survivor Annuity, Single Lump Sum.
  - Retirement Pension types: Normal, Early (409A), Late (409A), Disability, and Vested; related ages/dates: Normal Retirement Age (65 or later when 5 years Elapsed Time Service), Normal/Late Retirement Dates, Annuity Starting Date (with reemployment handling).
- Eligibility, employment, and service:
  - Participant, Employee/Employer (per Salaried Plan), Company and PepsiCo Organization (Code §414 controlled group).
  - Service constructs: Service, Credited Service, Elapsed Time Service (illustrated), Separation from Service under 409A (20% service threshold), leave-of-absence rules (6 months or protected period; 29 months for qualifying medical leaves), board service not counted toward separation.
- Spouse/domestic partner definitions:
  - Eligible Spouse (federal-law spouse; opposite-sex requirement only pre‑9/16/2013).
  - Eligible Domestic Partner (effective 1/1/2019 for active/authorized leave participants): civil union, health-benefit enrollment, or other written criteria; cannot have both spouse and domestic partner; only one partner at a time; “applicable date” is earlier of annuity start or death. Pre‑2019 rules in Appendix.
  - Pre-Retirement Spouse’s/Domestic Partner’s Pensions defined (including 409A portions).
- Earnings and Social Security measures:
  - Highest Average Monthly Earnings (Salaried Plan definition without 401(a)(17) cap) with special projection for severance-related leave earnings paid after separation.
  - Covered Compensation (per Salaried Plan), Primary Social Security Amount (assumptions for retirement/vested; actual initial disability benefit for disability; excludes spousal/dependent and post-separation changes), Taxable Wage Base.
- Key Employee (409A specified employee) identification:
  - Based on Code §416(i) officer/owner thresholds; annual determination each Dec 31 effective for 12 months starting April 1.
  - Administrative convenience: all Leadership Group 6+ also treated as Key Employees (subject to 200-person cap); transitional rules 2010–2018 across PepsiCo/PBG/PAS business classifications; special combination method for 2/26/2010–3/31/2010. Intended to comply with 409A specified employee rules.
- Governance and administration:
  - Plan, 409A Program vs Pre-409A Program; Plan Year; ERISA and Code references; Section 409A.
  - PepsiCo Administration Committee (PAC) as Plan Administrator: Chair is SVP Total Rewards (or functional successor), appoints four other experienced members per guiding principles; semiannual activity reporting to senior U.S.-based executives.
  - FICA Amount and Cashout Limit defined.
- Prohibited Misconduct:
  - Non-compete with “Covered Products,” employee non-solicitation, confidentiality breaches, acts contrary to company interests (e.g., Code of Conduct violations, insider trading), and fraud.
  - Carve-outs for lawful whistleblowing and Defend Trade Secrets Act immunity; broad “Participation” definition and expansive “Covered Products” list (beverages, snacks, cereals, pasta/rice, juices, related categories, and in-development products).
- Construction/interpretation rules:
  - Gender/number usage, “hereof/hereunder” refer to entire Plan, and “including” is non-limiting.
- Cross-references:
  - Frequent reliance on Salaried Plan provisions (definitions, factors) and Appendices for prior actuarial factors and pre‑2019 domestic partner rules.

- Normal 409A Retirement Pension: available upon Separation from Service after reaching Normal Retirement Age.

- Late 409A Retirement Pension: for participants who continue working past Normal Retirement Age; payments begin at the Late Retirement Date and are determined per Section 4.4 of Part B of the Salaried Plan (with certain exceptions noted but truncated in the excerpt).

summary:

- Surviving Eligible Spouses or Eligible Domestic Partners may receive survivor benefits; benefit amounts are determined under Article V.
- 4.1 Normal 409A Retirement Pension: Available if a participant Separates from Service after reaching Normal Retirement Age.
- 4.2 Early 409A Retirement Pension: Available if a participant Separates from Service before Normal Retirement Age, after reaching at least age 55 and completing 10 or more years of Elapsed Time Service.
- 4.3 409A Vested Pension: Available to participants vested under Section 4.7 who Separate from Service before qualifying for Normal or Early 409A Retirement Pensions; participants who terminate employment before meeting the vesting requirement are not eligible for any pension under the plan.
- 4.4 Late 409A Retirement Pension: For participants who continue working past Normal Retirement Age without a Separation from Service; pension begins at the Late Retirement Date and is determined in accordance with Section 4.4 of Part B of the Salaried Plan (with certain exclusions noted).

title: Late 409A Retirement Pension
heading: 4.4 Late 409A Retirement Pension
start_phrase: A Participant who continues without a Separation from Service after his Normal Retirement Age shall not receive a Pension until his Late Retirement Date.
summary:
- Article IV outlines eligibility requirements for pensions and certain survivor benefits under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program, with benefit amounts determined under Article V.
- Normal 409A Retirement Pension: Payable when a participant Separates from Service after reaching Normal Retirement Age.
- Early 409A Retirement Pension: Available upon Separation from Service after age 55 with at least 10 years of Elapsed Time Service but before Normal Retirement Age.
- 409A Vested Pension: Available to participants vested under Section 4.7 who separate before qualifying for Normal or Early 409A Retirement; those not vested under Section 4.7 are ineligible for any pension.
- Late 409A Retirement Pension: For participants who continue working past Normal Retirement Age; benefits begin at the Late Retirement Date and are determined per Part B, Section 4.4 of the Salaried Plan, without certain ERISA suspension notice or specific plan adjustments.
- 409A Disability Pension: Available if the participant meets disability criteria under Part B of the Salaried Plan; composed of (1) Pre-Separation Accruals (service up to Separation) and, if applicable, (2) Post-LTD Accruals (service credited after Separation due to disability) until the earliest of age 65, commencement under the Salaried Plan, or recovery.
- Pre-Retirement Spouse’s 409A Pension: Payable if the participant dies before the Annuity Starting Date; begins the first day of the month following the later of the participant’s death or when the participant would have turned 55, and continues for the Eligible Spouse’s lifetime (subject to Section 4.9). The subsection addressing Active, Disabled, and Retired Employees begins but is truncated.

title: 409A Disability Pension
heading: 4.5 409A Disability Pension
start_phrase: A Participant shall be eligible for a 409A Disability Pension if he meets the requirements for a Disability Pension under Part B of the Salaried Plan.
summary:
- References compliance with ERISA section 203(a)(3)(B) regarding notice of suspension of benefits and potential adjustments under Section 5.7(d) of Part B of the Salaried Plan.
- Section 4.5 outlines the 409A Disability Pension:
  - Eligibility aligns with the Disability Pension rules under Part B of the Salaried Plan.
  - Benefit is split into:
    - Pre-Separation Accruals: benefits based on Credited Service up to the Separation from Service date.
    - Post-LTD Accruals: benefits for Credited Service after Separation related to disability, accruing until the earliest of age 65, benefit commencement under Part B, or recovery from disability.
- Section 4.6 details the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s 409A Pension:
  - Payable only if the Participant dies before the Annuity Starting Date.
  - Commences the first day of the month after the later of the Participant’s death or the date the Participant attains/would have attained age 55.
  - Continues monthly for the life of the Eligible Spouse, subject to Section 4.9.
  - Applies to active, disabled, and retired employees (subsection (a) introduction).
text:
5    409A Disability Pension : A Participant shall be eligible for a 409A Disability Pension if he meets
the requirements for a Disability Pension under Part B of the Salaried Plan. A Participant’ s 409A Disability Pension, if
any, shall generally be comprised of two parts. The first part shall represent the benefits with respect to a disabled
Participant’ s Credited Service through the day of the Participant’ s Separation from Service ( i.e., the Participant’ s “Pre-
Separation Accruals”). In the event the disabled Participant continues to receive Credited Service related to the
disability after such Separation from Service, the Participant’ s 409A Disability Pension shall have a second part,
which shall represent all benefits accrued with respect to Credited Service from the date immediately following the
Participant’ s Separation from Service until the earliest of the Participant’ s (i) attainment of age 65, (ii) benefit
commencement date under Part B of the Salaried Plan or (iii) recovery from the disability ( i.e., the Participant’ s “Post-
LTD Accruals”).
4.

title: Pre-Retirement Spouse’s 409A Pension
heading: 4.6 Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s 409A Pension
start_phrase: A Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s 409A Pension is payable under this section only in the event the Participant dies prior to his Annuity Starting Date.
summary:
- Mentions compliance with ERISA section 203(a)(3)(B) (notice of suspension of benefits) and potential adjustments under Section 5.7(d) of Part B of the Salaried Plan.
- Section 4.5 (409A Disability Pension):

  - Benefit consists of two components:
    - Pre-Separation Accruals: benefits tied to Credited Service through the Participant’s Separation from Service.
    - Post-LTD Accruals: benefits tied to Credited Service after Separation due to disability, accruing until the earliest of age 65, commencement of Part B benefits, or recovery from disability.

title: Vesting
heading: 4.7 Vesting
start_phrase: Subject to Section 8.7 (Section 457A), a Participant shall be fully vested in, and have a nonforfeitable right to, his Accrued Benefit at the time he becomes fully vested in his accrued benefit under Part B of the Salaried Plan.
summary:
- Vesting: Participants become fully vested in their Accrued Benefit under the 409A Program when they are fully vested in their accrued benefit under Part B of the Salaried Plan, subject to Section 8.7 (Section 457A).
- Time of Payment: 409A Pension distributions begin at the time specified in Section 6.1 (subject to Section 6.6). Any interest attributable to payment delays under Salaried Plan Section 3.1(e) accrues entirely under the 409A Program and is paid at the same time and in the same form as the 409A Pension. Interest on delayed Pre‑409A Pension amounts is limited to what can be paid under 409A rules. No interest is paid for delays caused by the participant or if prohibited by an IRS 409A correction program.
- Cashout Distributions (small benefits): Notwithstanding other payment forms, special rules apply to small annuity benefits. If, at the Annuity Starting Date, the actuarial equivalent lump-sum value of a participant’s 409A Pension is at or below the Cashout Limit, the Plan Administrator will distribute a cashout (details continue beyond the excerpt).
- Document context: These provisions are part of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program, coordinating with the Salaried Plan and ensuring compliance with Internal Revenue Code sections 409A and 457A.

title: Time of Payment
heading: 4.8 Time of Payment
start_phrase: The distribution of a Participant’ s 409A Pension shall commence as of the time specified in Section 6.1, subject to Section 6.6.
summary:
- Vesting: Participants become fully vested in their Accrued Benefit under the 409A Program when they are fully vested in their accrued benefit under Part B of the Salaried Plan, subject to Section 8.7 (relating to Section 457A).
- Time of payment: 409A Pension distributions commence as specified in Section 6.1, subject to Section 6.6.
- Interest on delayed payments: Any interest attributable to a delay in payment under Part A, Section 3.1(e) of the Salaried Plan accrues entirely under the 409A Program and is paid at the same time and in the same form as the 409A Pension.
- Limits on interest: Interest adjustments for delayed payment of the Pre-409A Pension are restricted to amounts and timing permitted under Section 409A; no interest is payable if the delay is caused by the participant or if interest is barred by an IRS Section 409A correction program. These rules override contrary Salaried Plan provisions, including Part A, Section 3.1(e).
- Cashout distributions (small benefits): Despite other form-of-payment options in Article VI, small annuity benefits are subject to cashout rules; if the actuarial lump-sum value of a participant’s 409A Pension at the Annuity Starting Date does not exceed the Cashout Limit, the Plan Administrator will distribute a cashout (section continues with details).

title: Cashout Distributions
heading: 4.9 Cashout Distributions
start_phrase: Notwithstanding the availability or applicability of a dif ferent form of payment under Article VI, the following rules shall apply in the case of certain small benefit Annuity payments:
summary:
- Section 4.7 (Vesting): A participant becomes fully vested in the 409A Accrued Benefit when fully vested in the corresponding accrued benefit under Part B of the Salaried Plan, subject to Section 8.7 (Section 457A).
- Section 4.8 (Time of Payment): 409A Pension payments begin per Section 6.1, subject to any six-month delay in Section 6.6. Any interest due to delayed payment under Salaried Plan Part A, Section 3.1(e), accrues entirely under the 409A Program and is paid with the 409A Pension, only as permitted under Code Section 409A. No interest is paid for delays caused by the participant or prohibited by IRS correction programs.
- Section 4.9 (Cashout Distributions for small benefits):
  - Participant’s 409A Pension: If the actuarial lump sum value at the Annuity Starting Date is at or below the Cashout Limit (or $15,000 for Annuity Starting Dates before December 1, 2012), it is paid as a lump sum.
  - Pre-Retirement Spouse’s 409A Pension: Same small-benefit cashout rule (Cashout Limit, or $15,000 before December 1, 2012).
  - Special discretionary cashouts of 409A Vested Pensions: The Plan Administrator may cash out in a lump sum (i) on December 1, 2012, or (ii) on the first day of a month in 2013 or later years, if the benefit has not started, the lump sum value is at or below the Cashout Limit, and calculation/distribution is practicable; selections must be documented in writing by specified deadlines.
  - Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension: Lump sum cashout if the actuarial value is at or below the Cashout Limit.
  - Exception effective January 1, 2018: No cashout if the participant is eligible for a “PEP Kicker” or “Qualified Kicker” under a “Severance Program” (as defined in Appendix Article E).
  - Compliance provisions: Cashouts are intended as “limited cashouts” under Treas. Reg. §1.409A-3(j)(4)(v); the participant’s entire “accountable benefit” across all nonaccount balance 409A plans must be considered and fully cashed out; any required six-month delay still applies; no direct or indirect election is permitted by the participant, spouse, or domestic partner.
- Section 4.10 (Reemployment): If a participant already receiving an annuity under Section 6.1(b) is reemployed and re-eligible for Part B of the Salaried Plan, the existing 409A Pension continues in the same form; any additional 409A benefit accrued after reemployment is payable based on the subsequent Separation from Service.
- Section 4.11 (Forfeiture of Benefits): For Post-2008 Accruals, if the participant engages in Prohibited Misconduct before the second anniversary of Separation from Service, all such accruals are forfeited (including amounts previously paid), and the 409A Pension is adjusted with recovery of prior payments.
- Section 4.12 (Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension): Payable only if the participant dies before the Annuity Starting Date under either program; begins the first of the month following the later of the participant’s death or when the participant would have turned age 55, and is subject to the cashout rules in Section 4.9.

title: Reemployment of Certain Participants
heading: 4.10 Reemployment of Certain Participants
start_phrase: In the case of a current or former Participant who is receiving his Pension as an Annuity under Section 6.1(b), and who is reemployed and is eligible to re-participate in Part B of the Salaried Plan after his Annuity Starting Date, payment of his 409A Pension will continue to be paid in the same form as it was paid prior to his reemployment.
summary:
- Covers portions of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program addressing payment rules, forfeiture, and survivor benefits.
- Cash-out: Notes that a Participant’s 409A Pension or a Pre-Retirement Eligible Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension may be cashed out under a referenced section.
- Reemployment (Section 4.10): If a Participant already receiving an annuity under Section 6.1(b) is rehired and eligible to re-participate in Part B of the Salaried Plan after the annuity start date, payments continue in the same form; any additional 409A Pension earned during reemployment is payable based on the subsequent Separation from Service.
- Forfeiture (Section 4.11): For Post-2008 Accruals, if the Plan Administrator determines the Participant engaged in Prohibited Misconduct before the second anniversary of Separation from Service, all such accruals are forfeited (whether already paid, being paid, or payable), the 409A Pension is adjusted accordingly, and previously paid Post-2008 amounts are recoverable.
- Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension (Section 4.12): Payable only if the Participant dies before the annuity starting date under either the 409A or Pre-409A Program; benefit begins on the first day of the month following the later of the Participant’s death or the date the Participant reaches (or would have reached) age 55, subject to Section 4.9.

title: Forfeiture of Benefits
heading: 4.11 Forfeiture of Benefits
start_phrase: Effective beginning with benefits accrued after December 31, 2008 (“Post-2008 Accruals”), and notwithstanding any other provision of this Plan to the contrary , if the Plan Administrator determines that a Participant has engaged in Prohibited Misconduct at any time prior to the second anniversary of his or her Separation from Service, the Participant shall forfeit all Post-2008 Accruals (whether paid previously , being paid currently or payable in the future), and his or her 409A Pension shall be adjusted to reflect such forfeiture and previously paid Post-2008 Accruals shall be recovered.
summary: The excerpt outlines three main provisions of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program: (1) Reemployment rules for participants already receiving an annuity: if a participant is reemployed and eligible to re-participate in Part B of the Salaried Plan after their annuity start date, their 409A Pension continues in the same payment form, and any additional 409A Pension earned during reemployment is payable based on the subsequent separation from service. (2) Forfeiture due to Prohibited Misconduct: for benefits accrued after December 31, 2008, if the Plan Administrator determines the participant engaged in Prohibited Misconduct any time before the second anniversary of separation, all such post‑2008 accruals are forfeited, the 409A Pension is adjusted, and amounts previously paid are subject to recovery. (3) Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension: payable only if the participant dies before their annuity starting date under either the 409A or Pre‑409A program; payments begin on the first day of the month following the later of the participant’s death or the date the participant would have reached age 55, subject to the plan’s cash‑out and related provisions referenced in Section 4.9.

title: Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension
heading: 4.12 Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner ’s 409A Pension
start_phrase: A Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner ’s 409A Pension is payable under this section only in the event the Participant dies prior to his Annuity Starting Date under either the 409A Program or the Pre-409A Program.
summary:
- Reemployment rules: If a participant already receiving a 409A annuity is reemployed and re-eligible for Part B of the Salaried Plan, payments continue in the same form during reemployment; any additional 409A benefit earned is payable after the subsequent separation from service.
- Forfeiture for misconduct: Post-2008 Accruals are forfeited if the Plan Administrator determines the participant engaged in Prohibited Misconduct before the second anniversary of separation; previously paid Post-2008 amounts are recoverable and the 409A Pension is adjusted accordingly.
- Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension:
  - Payable only if the participant dies before the Annuity Starting Date under the 409A or Pre-409A program.
  - Commences the first day of the month after the later of the participant’s death or the date the participant would have turned 55, and continues for the life of the Eligible Domestic Partner, subject to any cashout rules in Section 4.9.
  - For active, disabled, and retired employees: Amount determined under Section 5.8, after applying Section 5.6, mirroring Part B survivor provisions.
  - For vested terminated employees: Same determination rules; if this coverage is elected/in effect, the participant’s pension under Section 5.2(b) is reduced by an annual charge based on attained age (with pro rata for partial years), and no reduction for coverage in the 180 days following termination. The schedule lists increasing annual percentage charges by age bands.
- Article V – Amount of Retirement Pension:
  - When payable, the 409A Pension is determined under Section 5.1 or 5.3, subject to plan freeze (Article I) and adjustments in Sections 4.6(b) and 5.4.
  - Section 5.1 formula (subject to Section 8.7 on Section 457A): 409A Pension = Total Pension − Salaried Plan Pension − Pre-409A Pension (not below zero).

title: Participant’s 409A Pension

start_phrase: Subject to Section 8.7 (Section 457A), a Participant’ s 409A Pension shall be determined as follows –
summary:
- Article V sets how a 409A Retirement Pension amount is determined when payable, referencing Sections 5.1 or 5.3, with adjustments under Sections 4.6(b) and 5.4, and subject to the plan freeze in Article I.
- Section 5.1 defines a Participant’s 409A Pension (subject to Section 8.7/Section 457A) as: Total Pension minus Salaried Plan Pension minus Pre-409A Pension, not below zero.
- The calculation basis must: apply early/late commencement factors as of the Annuity Starting Date; reflect the relative value of different payment forms; make actuarial-equivalent adjustments; follow Plan Administrator rules to account for timing/form of prior payments and prevent benefit duplication.
- For Annuity Starting Dates after December 31, 2018, the 409A Pension can include a makeup where the Participant’s Pre-409A Pension used harsher early reduction factors than the 2019 Salaried Plan Factors (including portions from the PEP Guarantee).
- Key definitions for Section 5.1:
  - Total Pension: the greater of (i) the Part B Salaried Plan pension ignoring IRC 401(a)(17) and 415 limits and ignoring the deferral adjustment in Part B Section 5.7(d), or (ii) the PEP Guarantee (Section 5.2); comparisons reflect relative value of payment forms.
  - Salaried Plan Pension: the pension under Part B of the Salaried Plan.
  - Pre-409A Pension: the amount determined under Section 5.6.
- Section 5.2 (PEP Guarantee):
  - Eligibility: applies only to Participants with at least $75,000 in 1988 pensionable earnings from an Employer; defines “1988 pensionable earnings” per the 1988 Salaried Plan and excludes pay from non-Employer periods.
  - Benefit determination: calculated under stated formulas with special rules; for those actively employed in a classification eligible for the Salaried Plan before July 1, 1975, the benefit is the greater of specified amounts (details continue beyond the excerpt).

title: PEP Guarantee
heading: 5.2 PEP Guarantee
start_phrase: A Participant who is eligible under subsection (a) below shall be entitled to a PEP Guarantee benefit determined under subsection (b) below .
summary:
- Defines key terms used in benefit calculations: “Salaried Plan Pension” (as determined under Part B of the Salaried Plan) and “Pre-409A Pension” (as determined under Section 5.6).
- Establishes the PEP Guarantee:
  - Eligibility: Applies only to Participants with at least $75,000 in 1988 pensionable earnings from an Employer (as defined under the 1988 Salaried Plan rules; excludes pay from entities when not an Employer).
  - Benefit determination: Uses specified formulas, with special rules.
    - Formula A: 3% of Highest Average Monthly Earnings (HAME) for first 10 years of Credited Service + 1% of HAME for each additional year, minus 1-2/3% of Primary Social Security Amount times years of Credited Service up to 30. For a Vested Pension, first project service to Normal Retirement Age using HAME and Social Security at separation, then prorate by actual service over projected service.
    - Formula B (for those in an eligible Salaried Plan classification before July 1, 1975): Pension is the greater of (A) 1.5% of HAME × years of Credited Service − 50% of Primary Social Security Amount, or (B) 3% of HAME × years of Credited Service up to 15 − 50% of Primary Social Security Amount. For Disability Pensions, use Credited Service per the Salaried Plan and HAME/Social Security at disability date. For Vested Pensions, a stated subparagraph does not apply.
  - Special calculation rules:
    - Automatic 50% survivor annuity for an Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner with no reduction to the Participant’s annuity; if the survivor is more than 10 years younger, reduce the survivor benefit by 0.8% per full year from 11–20 years younger and an additional 0.4% per full year beyond 20.
    - Reductions for:
      - Early retirement: 3/12 of 1% (0.25%) per month before Normal Retirement Date.
      - Vested Pensions: actuarial equivalence if commencing early and specified reductions for pre-retirement spouse/domestic partner coverage.
      - Elected forms with higher survivor benefits than 50%: reduce to actuarial equivalence of the standard benefit.
      - Non-spouse/domestic partner survivor forms: reduce to the actuarial equivalent of a single life annuity.
      - Inflation-protected annuities: reduce to the actuarial equivalent of the same annuity without inflation protection.
    - Lump sum conversion: Lump sum equals the actuarial equivalent of the PEP Guarantee, reflecting survivor benefits and early retirement reductions.
    - Actuarial equivalence standard: Intended to preserve substantially the value of pre-1989 plan benefits and conform to Section 409A rules, including the Treasury regulation for subsidized joint and survivor annuities.
- Sets the Pre-Retirement Spouse’s 409A Pension amount:
  - Calculation: Equals the Total Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension minus the Salaried Plan’s Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension, further reduced (not below zero) by any portion derived from the Pre-409A Program.
  - Basis: Applies appropriate early/late commencement reductions and other actuarial equivalence adjustments as determined by the Plan Administrator, considering time and form of any prior payments.
  - Notes that definitions specific to this section apply (not shown in the excerpt).

heading: 5.3 Amount of Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s 409A Pension
start_phrase: The monthly amount of the Pre-Retirement Spouse’ s 409A Pension payable to a surviving Eligible Spouse under Section 4.6 shall be determined under subsection (a) below .
summary:
- Establishes how a surviving Eligible Spouse’s “Pre-Retirement Spouse’s 409A Pension” is calculated, coordinated with Section 409A (including the special rule for subsidized joint and survivor annuities).
- Calculation formula: Eligible Spouse’s Total Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension minus (i) the Salaried Plan Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension and (ii) the portion derived from the Pre-409A Program, floored at zero.
- Requires timing and actuarial adjustments: accounts for early/late commencement and applies Actuarial Equivalence and Plan Administrator rules, including consideration of prior payments and form of payment.
- Definitions:
  - Total Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension is the greater of (a) the Part B Salaried Plan pre-retirement spouse’s pension ignoring Code §§401(a)(17) and 415 limits and a specified actuarial adjustment, or (b) the PEP Guarantee Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension; determined as if payable at the Participant’s Normal Retirement Date, then adjusted for actual commencement timing.
  - Salaried Plan Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension: the amount under the Salaried Plan.
  - Pre-409A Program portion: the amount under the Pre-409A Program.
- PEP Guarantee Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension (by reference to Section 5.2):
  - Normal rule: equal to the survivor annuity under a QJSA as if the Participant separated at death (or earlier actual separation), commenced the QJSA at the survivor benefit start date, and died the next day.
  - Special rule for active/disabled employees (Section 4.6(a)): minimum 25% of the Participant’s PEP Guarantee; Credited Service per Part B Section 3.3(c)(2); Highest Average Monthly Earnings, Primary Social Security Amount, and Covered Compensation measured at death; no early commencement reduction.
  - Applies principles similar to Section 5.1(b) and the last sentence of Section 5.2(b)(2).
- Certain Adjustments (Section 5.4):
  - Defines “specified plan” as the Salaried Plan or similar nonqualified plans within the PepsiCo Organization not based on participant pay deferrals.
  - Rehired participants: if reemployed after Annuity Starting Date and Salaried Plan benefits are recalculated for additional service, the PEP Pension is recalculated to the maximum extent allowed under Section 409A; PEP Guarantee is adjusted for in-service and prior distributions consistent with the Salaried Plan while accounting for this Plan and any specified plans.
  - Provides for adjustments when pensions under other specified plans are increased after PEP benefits are determined (text partially truncated).

title: Certain Adjustments
heading: 5.4 Certain Adjustments
start_phrase: Pensions determined under the foregoing sections of this Article are subject to adjustment as provided in this section.
summary:
- Sets rules for a Pre-Retirement Spouse’s Pension: Covered Compensation measured as of the participant’s date of death; no early commencement reduction; determination of the spouse’s 409A Pension follows principles akin to Section 5.1(b) and the last sentence of Section 5.2(b)(2).
- Establishes “Certain Adjustments” to pensions, defining a “specified plan” as the Salaried Plan or a similar nonqualified plan (sponsored by a PepsiCo entity and not based on employee deferrals).
- Rehired participants: If the Salaried Plan benefit is recalculated after the Annuity Starting Date due to additional Credited Service, the PEP Pension (and PEP Guarantee) is correspondingly recalculated, accounting for in-service/prior distributions and benefits under this and specified plans, to the maximum extent permitted by Section 409A.
- Increases under other plans: If a specified plan later increases a participant’s benefit (e.g., by court order or administrator action), the PEP benefit is recalculated under Section 409A; any overpayment is subject to recovery; aims to prevent duplicative payments across this Plan and specified plans.
- No offsets violating Section 409A (effective Jan 1, 2009): Non-duplication/transfer rules from the Salaried Plan apply to Total Pension calculations only if they do not change the time or form of 409A payments; the Company intends to implement legally permissible, 409A-compliant coordination under qualifying plans to avoid prohibited changes, in which case offset limits do not apply.

summary: This excerpt from the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program covers three topics. First, Excludable Employment (Section 5.5) allows executives to sign written agreements waiving eligibility or agreeing not to participate in the Plan, with such waivers effective whether signed before or after eligibility/participation and applicable to agreements entered on or after January 1, 2009. Second, Pre-409A Pension (Section 5.6) defines the grandfathered portion of a participant’s pension under Treasury Regulation §1.409A-6(a)(3)(i) and (iv) and states it will be determined using principles parallel to those in Sections 5.1(b) and the last sentence of 5.2(b)(2). Third, Offsets (Section 5.7) permits the Company to reduce plan payments by amounts the participant owes the Company if the debt arose during employment, within Code Section 409A limits, and with reductions timed to when the debt would otherwise be due; it also addresses coordination where a participant has multiple 409A benefits with different payment timings.

summary:

- Section 5.5 (Excludable Employment): Executives who sign written agreements waiving eligibility or agreeing not to participate cannot later claim benefits or benefit increases from that employment. Such agreements can be executed before or after eligibility/participation, may take any effective form, and apply to agreements entered into on or after January 1, 2009.

- Section 5.7 (Offsets): Allows the Company to reduce plan payments by amounts the participant owes the Company if the debt arose during employment, within Code §409A limits, and with reductions timed and sized to match when the debt would have been due and collectible. title: Offsets
heading: 5.7 Offsets
start_phrase: Notwithstanding any other provision of the Plan, the Company may reduce the amount of any payment or benefit that is or would be payable to or on behalf of a Participant by the amount of any obligation of the Participant to the Company that is or becomes due and payable, provided that (1) the obligation of the Participant to the Company was incurred during the employment relationship, (2) the reduction during any Plan Y ear may not exceed the amount allowed under Code Section 409A and (3) the reduction is made at the same time and in the same amount as the obligation otherwise would have been due and collectable from the Participant.
summary:
- Excludable Employment (Sec. 5.5): Executives who sign written agreements waiving eligibility or agreeing not to participate in the Plan are permanently barred from receiving benefits or benefit increases tied to that employment. Such agreements can be executed before or after eligibility/participation, may take any effective form, and apply to agreements entered on or after January 1, 2009.
- Pre-409A Pension (Sec. 5.6): Defines the portion of a Participant’s Pension that is grandfathered under Treasury Regulation §1.409A-6(a)(3)(i) and (iv). Its determination follows principles referenced in Sections 5.1(b) and the last sentence of 5.2(b)(2).
- Offsets (Sec. 5.7): The Company may reduce payments/benefits by amounts the Participant owes the Company if incurred during employment, within Code §409A limits, and timed to when the debt would have been collectible. Additional 409A Benefits must also be offset by any Prior 409A Benefits, with the offset calculated at the annuity starting date, reflecting early/late commencement factors, relative value of payment forms where applicable, and actuarial equivalence under Plan Administrator rules (e.g., Pre-Separation Accruals offset Post-Disability Accruals).
- Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension (Sec. 5.8): For a surviving Eligible Domestic Partner (per Sec. 4.12), the monthly benefit equals the Total Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner’s Pension minus the Salaried Plan component, then further reduced (not below zero) by the portion derived from the Pre-409A Program.

heading: 5.8 Amount of Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner ’s Pension
start_phrase: The monthly amount of the Pre-Retirement Domestic Partner ’s 409A Pension payable to a surviving Eligible Domestic Partner under Section 4.12 shall be determined under subsection (a) below .
summary:
- Offsets of additional 409A Benefits: Any additional 409A benefit is reduced by the Prior 409A Benefit as of the annuity starting date, reflecting early/late commencement factors, relative value of payment forms, and actuarial equivalence per Plan Administrator rules; example given where Pre‑Separation Accruals offset Post‑Disability Accruals.
- Pre‑Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension (Section 5.8):
  - Calculation: Equals (a) Total Pre‑Retirement Domestic Partner’s Pension minus (b) the amount provided under the Salaried Plan, then minus (c) the portion derived from the Pre‑409A Program, floored at zero.
  - Determination basis: Applies early/late commencement adjustments and actuarial equivalence; Plan Administrator may adjust to reflect time/form of any prior payments.
  - Key definitions:
    - “Total” amount is the greater of: (i) the Salaried Plan benefit ignoring Code §§401(a)(17) and 415 limits and a specified actuarial adjustment, or (ii) the PEP Guarantee‑based Pre‑Retirement Domestic Partner’s 409A Pension; first compared at the Participant’s Normal Retirement Date, then adjusted for earlier/later commencement.
    - “Salaried Plan” amount and “Pre‑409A Program” amount are the respective plan‑determined benefits.
  - PEP Guarantee rules:
    - Normal rule: Benefit equals the survivor annuity under a hypothetical QJSA if the Participant separated at death (or earlier separation date), commenced the QJSA when the survivor benefit begins, and died the next day.
    - Special rule for active/disabled: Minimum of 25% of the Participant’s PEP Guarantee; Credited Service and compensation/SSA measures determined as of death; no early commencement reduction. Principles akin to Sections 5.1(b) and the last sentence of 5.2(b)(2) apply.
- Article VI — Distribution of Benefits:
  - Governs distributions of 409A Pensions and continuation to beneficiaries.
  - Pre‑Retirement Spouse’s/Domestic Partner’s Pensions under the 409A Program are paid as life annuities (subject to cashout rules); Pre‑409A Pension distributions follow the Pre‑409A Program.
  - Form/timing (Section 6.1):
    - Default: 409A Retirement Pension paid as a single lump sum on the first day of the month on/after the Retirement Date, subject to key employee delay.
    - Prior elections: Grandfathered payment elections made by December 31, 2007 (and at least six months before, in a prior calendar year) control form/timing of payment.

title: Form and Timing of Distributions
heading: 6.1 Form and T iming of Distributions
start_phrase: Benefits under the 409A Program shall be distributed as follows:
summary:
- Scope: Article VI governs how benefits under the 409A Program are distributed to participants and, if applicable, continued to beneficiaries after a participant’s death. Pre-Retirement Spouse’s/Domestic Partner’s Pensions from the 409A Program are paid as life annuities (subject to cashout rules in Section 4.9). Distributions of Pre-409A Pensions follow the Pre-409A Program rules.
- 409A Retirement Pension (Section 6.1(a)):
  - Default: Single lump sum on the first day of the month coincident with or next following the Retirement Date, subject to the Key Employee delay (Section 6.6) and cashouts (Section 4.9).
  - Prior elections: If a participant made a valid payment election by December 31, 2007 and at least six months before (and in a prior calendar year to) the Annuity Starting Date, the benefit is paid per that election (annuity and/or alternative commencement date). Elections are disregarded if the participant only qualifies for a Vested Pension at Separation.
  - Annuity defaults if elected: Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity (QJSA) if married; Single Life Annuity if unmarried, unless an optional form under Section 6.2 is elected per procedures in Section 6.3(a). Marital status is determined on the Annuity Starting Date.
  - Late commencement due to an election increases the benefit for earnings using the plan’s actuarial interest rate through the payment check date.
- 409A Vested Pension (Section 6.1(b); subject to Sections 4.9 and 6.6):
  - Separation before age 55 with at least 5 years of Service: Annuity begins on the first of the month coincident with or following age 55 (Annuity Starting Date).
  - Separation at ages 55–64 with at least 5 but less than 10 years of Service: Annuity begins on the first of the month following Separation.
  - Default forms: QJSA if married; Single Life if unmarried. An unmarried participant with an Eligible Domestic Partner may elect a 50% or 75% Survivor Annuity with the partner as beneficiary (per Section 6.2). Marital/partner status measured at the Annuity Starting Date. Optional forms may be elected under Section 6.2 following Section 6.3(a) procedures.
- 409A Disability Pension (Section 6.1(c)):
  - Pre-Separation Accruals: Paid on the first day of the month following the later of age 55 or Separation; available forms mirror those for Vested or Retirement Pensions under Section 6.2 (with distinctions for married/domestic partner vs. single).
  - Post-LTD Accruals: Paid as a lump sum on the first day of the month following attainment of age 65.
- Available Forms of Payment (Section 6.2):
  - Applies to Retirement Pensions subject to a valid prior election (Section 6.1(a)(2)) and to Vested Pensions (Section 6.1(b)).
  - Retirement Pension: Participant may choose among optional forms by valid election per Section 6.3(a).
  - Vested Pension: If married on the Annuity Starting Date, the participant may elect only certain specified optional forms (paragraph (1), (2)(ii), or (2)(iii)) with the Eligible Spouse as beneficiary; if not married but with an Eligible Domestic Partner, designated optional forms are available. Further details continue beyond the excerpt.
- Cross-references: Cashout distributions (Section 4.9), election procedures (Section 6.3(a)), and Key Employee payment delay (Section 6.6).

title: Available Forms of Payment
heading: 6.2 Available Forms of Payment
start_phrase: This section sets forth the payment options available to a Participant who is entitled to a Retirement Pension under paragraph 6.1(a)(2) above or a V ested Pension under subsection 6.1(b) above.
summary:
- Defines Disability Pension payment timing under the 409A Program:
  - Pre-Separation Accruals: paid starting the first day of the month after the later of age 55 or Separation from Service; payable in the same optional forms available for Vested or Retirement Pensions (Section 6.2), with options varying by marital/domestic partner status.
  - Post-LTD Accruals: paid as a lump sum on the first day of the month following attainment of age 65.
- Specifies available forms of payment for Retirement and Vested Pensions (Section 6.2):
  - Eligibility constraints:
    - Retirement Pension: may elect any optional form per Section 6.3(a).
    - Vested Pension:
      - Married at Annuity Starting Date: may elect Single Life, 75% Survivor, or 50% Survivor with Eligible Spouse as beneficiary; no other forms.
      - Not married with Eligible Domestic Partner: may elect 75% or 50% Survivor with the partner as beneficiary; no other forms.
      - Not married and no Eligible Domestic Partner: must receive a Single Life Annuity.
    - All optional annuities are actuarially equivalent to a Single Life Annuity.
  - Optional forms:
    - Single Life Annuity: monthly payments end at death.
    - Survivor Options: reduced lifetime benefit to participant, then to beneficiary for life at:
      - 100% continuation,
      - 75% continuation,
      - 50% continuation (Qualified Joint and Survivor Annuity if beneficiary is Eligible Spouse).
    - Ten Years Certain and Life: reduced lifetime benefit with at least 120 monthly payments; remaining guaranteed payments go to primary (or contingent) beneficiary if the participant dies before 120 payments.
- Provides optional inflation protection for annuities:
  - 5% or 7% thresholds: benefit initially reduced; annual increases apply only if prior-year inflation exceeds the elected threshold, equal to the excess over 5% or 7%.
  - Adjustments occur each January 1 starting with the second January 1 after the Annuity Starting Date.
  - Inflation measured over the 12 months ending September 30, using the same methodology as Social Security COLAs in effect on the plan’s Effective Date.
  - Inflation protection carries over to survivor benefits and is irrevocable once elected.
- Outlines procedures for Annuity Starting Date elections (Section 6.3):
  - Details how to make valid elections for optional forms (subsection (a)) and special rules for multiple Annuity Starting Dates (subsection (b)).
  - An election is deemed received on the date it is postmarked or actually received by the Plan Administrator.

title: Procedures for Elections
heading: 6.3 Procedures for Elections
start_phrase: This section sets forth the procedures for making Annuity Starting Date elections ( i.e., elections under Section 6.2).
summary:
- Inflation protection options: Participants can elect 5% or 7% inflation protection. Monthly benefits are initially reduced, then increased annually if the prior year’s inflation exceeds the elected threshold, by the amount over 5% or 7%.
- Timing and measurement: Increases apply each January 1 starting with the second January 1 after the Annuity Starting Date. Inflation is measured over the 12 months ending September 30, using the same method as Social Security COLAs in effect on the plan’s Effective Date.
- Survivor benefits and irrevocability: Elected inflation protection carries over to survivor benefits. Elections of inflation protection are irrevocable by the participant or surviving beneficiary.
- Election procedures (Section 6.3): Defines how and when Annuity Starting Date elections are made and deemed received (postmark or actual receipt by close of business). Spousal consent is not required.
- Optional form election requirements: Must be in writing, signed, and received at least one day before the Annuity Starting Date; must specify the payment form and any beneficiary per Section 6.5. Electronic elections and affirmations may be accepted if permitted by the Plan Administrator.
- Multiple Annuity Starting Dates: Elections at an Annuity Starting Date apply to all unpaid accruals then due. For rehired participants who continue an annuity in pay status or previously received a lump sum (other than a specific cashout), a later Annuity Starting Date and elections apply only to benefits accrued after rehire; earlier accruals continue under prior elections.
- Marital status determination (effective Jan 1, 2014): Participant is presumed unmarried on the Annuity Starting Date unless the participant provides satisfactory advance notice of being married; the Plan Administrator may adopt different rules.
- Survivor options (Section 6.4): Introduces special rules for survivor options, beginning with effects of certain deaths when an optional annuity with survivor benefits has been elected (details continue beyond the excerpt).
