title: Special Rules for Survivor Options
heading: 6.4 Special Rules for Survivor Options
start_phrase: The following special rules shall apply for the survivor options available under Section 6.2.
summary:
- Rehire and subsequent Annuity Starting Date elections: New elections after a subsequent Separation from Service apply only to benefits accrued after rehire; prior unpaid accruals continue under the original elections made at the initial Annuity Starting Date.
- Marital status determination (effective January 1, 2014): Participant is presumed unmarried on the Annuity Starting Date unless satisfactory advance notice of marriage is provided to the Plan. Notice is given with the form election or via Plan Administrator procedures. The Plan Administrator may adopt different rules.
- Special survivor option rules (Section 6.2):
  - Death timing effects: If the Participant or beneficiary dies before the Annuity Starting Date, the survivor-option election is disregarded. If the Participant dies after the Annuity Starting Date but before payments actually commence, the elected survivor form applies; survivor payments start the first day of the month following death, with any back payments to the Participant’s estate.
  - 120-payment feature (Section 6.2(a)(2)(iv)): If the Participant dies after the Annuity Starting Date without a surviving primary or contingent beneficiary and before 120 payments are made, remaining payments go to the Participant’s estate. If payments to a beneficiary have begun and that beneficiary dies before completion, remaining payments go to that beneficiary’s estate.
  - Age difference limits for non-spouse/partner beneficiaries: The 100% survivor option is unavailable if the beneficiary is more than 10 years younger than the Participant; the 75% survivor option is unavailable if the beneficiary is more than 19 years younger.
- Beneficiary designation requirements: Participants electing a survivor form must designate beneficiaries on the applicable election form (may name primary and contingent for Section 6.2(a)(2)(iv)). Changes/revocations are allowed until the Annuity Starting Date and are effective upon filing per Plan rules. If no valid designation exists for a survivor option, the default beneficiary is the Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner. Participants entitled only to a Vested Pension cannot name a beneficiary; if an optional form is allowed, the beneficiary is the Eligible Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner on the Annuity Starting Date.
- Key Employee distribution delay (Section 409A): For Participants classified as Key Employees at Separation from Service (or other applicable determination time), 409A Retirement Pension payments begin on the earliest first day of a month at least six months after Separation from Service, or earlier upon the Participant’s death.

title: Payment of FICA and Related Income Taxes
heading: 6.7 Payment of FICA and Related Income T axes
start_phrase: As provided in subsections (a) through (c) below , a portion of a Participant’ s 409A Pension shall be paid as a single lump sum and remitted directly to the Internal Revenue Service (“IRS”) in satisfaction of the Participant’ s FICA Amount and the related withholding of income tax at source on wages (imposed under Code Section 3401 or the corresponding withholding provisions of the applicable state, local or foreign tax laws as a result of the payment of the FICA Amount) and the additional withholding of income tax at source on wages that is attributable to the pyramiding of wages and taxes.
summary:
- Section 6.7 (Payment of FICA and Related Income Taxes): A portion of a Participant’s 409A Pension is paid as a single lump sum and remitted directly to the IRS to cover the Participant’s FICA tax, related income tax withholding triggered by that FICA payment, and any additional withholding due to pyramiding.
- Timing (6.7(a)): The lump sum equal to the FICA Amount and related income tax withholding is paid from the Participant’s 409A Pension and deposited with the IRS when those taxes are due; Key Employee status does not affect this timing.
- Pension Reduction (6.7(b)): The Participant’s 409A Pension is reduced by the actuarial equivalent of the lump-sum tax payment, effective as of the tax payment date; this reduction may occur after pension payments have already begun.
- No Effect on Pension Commencement (6.7(A)): The tax-related lump-sum payment does not alter the commencement date or schedule of the Participant’s (actuarially reduced) 409A Pension, including any required delay for Key Employees.

The Company and Plan Administrator are not fiduciaries, and ERISA section 406 party-in-interest restrictions do not apply.
- Facility of Payment (7.2): If a payee is under legal disability or otherwise incapacitated, the Plan Administrator may pay the individual, their legal representative, or apply payments for their benefit; such payments discharge the Plan’s liability.
- Claims Procedure (7.3): The Plan Administrator (or its designee) holds exclusive discretionary authority to construe and interpret the Plan (section begins in the excerpt).

title: Authority to Administer Plan
heading: 7.1 Authority to Administer Plan
start_phrase: The Plan shall be administered by the Plan Administrator , which shall have the authority to interpret the Plan and issue such regulations as it deems appropriate.
summary:
- Article VII (Administration) of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program outlines governance and administrative powers.
- The Plan Administrator has broad authority to administer the Plan, interpret provisions, issue regulations, maintain records, and calculate benefits, relying on participant-provided information (e.g., address, age, marital status). Its interpretations and determinations are final and binding.
- Neither the Company nor the Plan Administrator is a fiduciary of the Plan, and ERISA Section 406 party-in-interest restrictions do not apply to the Plan, including with respect to the Company and the Plan Administrator.
- Facility of Payment: If a payee is under legal disability or otherwise incapacitated, the Plan Administrator may pay the individual, their legal representative, or apply payments for their benefit; such payments fully discharge the Plan’s liability for those amounts.
- Claims Procedure: The Plan Administrator, or its designee, holds exclusive discretionary authority to construe and interpret the Plan (section text is partially truncated).

title: Claims Procedure
heading: 7.3 Claims Procedure
start_phrase: The Plan Administrator , or a party designated by the Plan Administrator , shall have the exclusive discretionary authority to construe and to interpret the Plan, to decide all questions of eligibility for benefits and to determine the amount of such benefits.
summary:
- Establishes that the Plan Administrator has broad, final, and binding authority to interpret the Plan, issue regulations, maintain records, calculate benefits, and rely on participant-provided information (e.g., address, age, marital status).
- States that neither the Company nor the Plan Administrator is a fiduciary under the Plan, and ERISA section 406 party-in-interest restrictions do not apply to the Plan, the Company, or the Plan Administrator.
- Provides “facility of payment” rules allowing the Plan Administrator to direct payments to or for the benefit of a person under legal disability or incapacity (including to a legal representative), with such payments fully discharging Plan liability.
- Details an expansive claims and appeals process:
  - The Plan Administrator (or its designee) has exclusive, absolute discretion to interpret the Plan, determine eligibility and benefit amounts, and consider the Company’s intent; benefits are payable only if the Administrator so decides.
  - Any review by a court is under the arbitrary and capricious (abuse of discretion) standard.

title: Claimant Must Exhaust the Plan’s Claims Procedures Before Filing in Court
heading: 7.5 Claimant Must Exhaust the Plan’ s Claims Procedures Before Filing in Court
start_phrase: Before filing any Claim (including a suit or other action) in court or in another tribunal, a Claimant must first fully exhaust all of the Claimant’ s rights under the claims procedures of Section 7.3.
summary:
- Mandatory exhaustion of the Plan’s internal claims procedures (Section 7.3) before filing any lawsuit or tribunal action; exhaustion is to be enforced as broadly as possible.
- Exhaustion is not excused unless a claimant clearly submitted a claim or properly requested documents under strict conditions (written request to and received by the Plan Administrator, ERISA entitlement, six-month response window or reasonable extension, clear assertion of ERISA rights/entitlement, and materiality to a colorable claim). Individuals not treated as Participants must clearly assert participant entitlement.
- After exhaustion, any court or tribunal review is limited, to the maximum extent permitted, to the administrative record before the Plan Administrator.
- Exhaustion applies even when:
  - Other non-claim disputes are more significant or are considered concurrently.
  - Rights are novel, discretionary, actual, or potential.
  - No specific claims procedures exist for the issue (the Plan Administrator will establish or analogize to Section 7.3 procedures).
- The Plan Administrator may create special procedures for class claims or conflict situations to preserve the exhaustion requirement.
- Broad definitions:
  - Dispute: any claim, dispute, issue, assertion, action, or other matter.
  - Claim: any Dispute involving Plan interpretation, terms, validity, administration, alleged ERISA/legal violations, benefit requests/recoveries, fiduciary breach assertions, or any related matters as deemed by the Plan Administrator.
  - Claimant: broadly includes actual or putative employees/participants, former participants, beneficiaries and related parties (spouses, former spouses, domestic partners, estates, heirs, representatives), and groups thereof.
- Statement of intent to operate consistent with ERISA and to impose a contractual obligation of complete exhaustion to ensure efficient, uniform resolution and limit unnecessary litigation costs.
- Two-year limitations period (Section 7.6) for:
  - Benefit denial claims under Section 7.3 and court actions alleging wrongful denial or interference/violation of ERISA-protected rights.
  - Accrual for benefit claims: the earliest of receipt of the benefit calculation, the identified payment start date, actual or constructive knowledge of operative facts, or the first payment/provision/denial.
  - Accrual for ERISA interference claims: when the claimant has actual or constructive knowledge of the alleged interfering acts or facts.

heading: 7.6 Limitations on Actions
start_phrase: Any claim filed under section 7.3 and any action filed in state or federal court by or on behalf of a former or current Employee, Participant, beneficiary or any other individual, person or entity (collectively , a “Petitioner”) for the alleged wrongful denial of Plan benefits or for the alleged interference with or violation of ERISA-protected rights must be brought within two years of the date the Petitioner ’s cause of action first accrues.
summary:
- Defines “Claimant” broadly to include any current or former employee or participant, their beneficiaries (including spouses, former spouses, domestic partners), estates, heirs, representatives, related entities or individuals, and groups thereof, who have a claim under the plan.
- Establishes a two-year statute of limitations (Section 7.6) for:
  - Claims under the plan’s internal claims/appeals process (Section 7.3) and court actions alleging wrongful denial of benefits or interference with ERISA rights.
  - “Petitioner” includes any current or former employee, participant, beneficiary, or any other individual, person, or entity bringing such claims.
- Specifies accrual rules for the two-year period:
  - Benefit claims: accrue at the earliest of (i) receipt of the benefit calculation, (ii) the payment commencement date identified by the Plan Administrator, (iii) when the claimant has actual or constructive knowledge of the relevant acts/omissions or facts, or (iv) when the benefit was first paid, provided, or denied.
  - ERISA interference claims: accrue when the claimant has actual or constructive knowledge of the acts/omissions or facts constituting the alleged interference.
  - Other claims: must be brought within two years of when the claimant has actual or constructive knowledge of the acts/omissions or facts giving rise to the claim.
- Failure to file within two years bars the claim; communications during or after the mandatory appeal process do not extend or toll this deadline.
- Restricts venue (Section 7.7): all court or tribunal actions related to the plan must be filed exclusively in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York for claims filed on or after January 1, 2011.

violation of ERISA-protected rights must be brought within two years of the date the Petitioner ’s cause of action first

the Plan shall be deemed to accrue not later than the earliest of (i) when the Petitioner has received the
calculation of the benefits that are the subject of the claim or legal action, (ii) the date identified to the
Petitioner by the Plan Administrator on which payments shall commence, (iii) when the Petitioner has actual or
constructive knowledge of the acts or failures to act (or the other facts) that are the basis of his claim, or (iv)
the date when the benefit was first paid, provided, or denied.
(b) For purposes of this subsection, a cause of action with respect to the alleged interference
with ERISA-protected rights shall be deemed to accrue when the claimant has actual or constructive
knowledge of the acts or failures to act (or the other facts) that are alleged to constitute interference with
ERISA-protected rights.

title: Section 457A
heading: 8.7 Section 457A
start_phrase: To avoid the application of Code section 457A (“Section 457A”) to a Participant’ s Pension, the following shall apply to a Participant who transfers to a work location outside of the United States to provide services to a member of the PepsiCo Organization that is neither a United States corporation nor a pass- through entity that is wholly owned by a United States corporation (“Covered T ransfer”):
summary:
The excerpt outlines administrative and compliance provisions of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program:

- Anti-duplication of benefits: If any compensation element is or could be recognized elsewhere under the Plan (including through integration with the Salaried Plan), the specific governing provision controls and duplicate recognition is prohibited.

- Section 457A compliance for international assignments: For Participants who transfer to non-U.S. entities within the PepsiCo Organization that are neither U.S. corporations nor wholly owned pass-throughs (“Covered Transfer”):
  - Automatic vesting occurs as of the last business day before the transfer.
  - Post-transfer benefit enhancements tied to service or age attainment (“Benefit Enhancement”) are not credited until the last day of the Plan Year and only to the extent permissible; Participants have no legal right to enhancements that would be includable in income under Section 457A.
  - The Company may issue an “applicable communication” overriding these rules for a given transfer.
  - The deferred-credit rule ceases when the Participant returns to a qualifying U.S. entity or as otherwise specified in an applicable communication.

- Authorized transfers outside the PepsiCo Organization: Liability for benefits accrued while employed by PepsiCo remains with the Company unless an agreement with the new employer provides otherwise.

- Electronic signatures and records: Electronic signatures and electronic recordkeeping are authorized and have the same legal effect, validity, and enforceability as manual signatures and paper records.

- All amendment and termination actions must comply with Internal Revenue Code Section 409A; the Company’s authority is as broad as law permits.
- Continuation: The Company intends to maintain the Plan indefinitely but has no obligation to do so and may amend, terminate, or partially terminate at any time. - Amendments: The Company alone may amend the Plan, with or without retroactive effect, including to ensure 409A compliance; other Employers cannot amend.

These terms are the exclusive basis for distributions related to Change in Control for benefits under this 409A Program.

- Effective July 1, 1996, the program is divided into three separate ERISA plans; prior to that date, the plans described in (b) and (c) were combined as a single ERISA plan.
- Excess Benefit Plan (ERISA §3(36)): Provides benefits to Salaried Plan participants that exceed the Internal Revenue Code §415 limits.
- Excess Compensation Top Hat Plan: A “top hat” plan for a select group of management or highly compensated employees (ERISA §§201(2), 401(a)(1)), providing benefits above the IRC §401(a)(17) compensation limits under the Salaried Plan, after considering benefits from the Excess Benefit Plan; for ERISA reporting, this portion may be called the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan I.
- Preservation Top Hat Plan: Another “top hat” plan for a select group of management or highly compensated employees (ERISA §§201(2), 401(a)(1)), intended to preserve certain benefits for Salaried Plan participants (details truncated in the excerpt).

Effective during the T ransition Period, the language of Section 8.6(a) shall be replaced in its entirety with the
following language:
“8.6(a)    Compliance with Section 409A :
At all times during each Plan Y ear, this Plan shall be operated (i) in accordance with the requirements of
Section 409A, and (ii) to preserve the status of deferrals under the Pre-409A Program as being exempt from
Section 409A, i.e., to preserve the grandfathered status of the Pre-409A Program. Any action that may be
taken (and, to the extent possible, any action actually taken) by the Plan Administrator or the Company shall
not be taken (or shall be void and without ef fect), if such action violates the requirements of Section 409A or if
such action would adversely af fect the grandfather of the Pre-409A Program. If the failure to take an action
under the Plan would violate Section 409A, then to the extent it is possible thereby to avoid a violation of
Section 409A, the rights and ef fects under the Plan shall be altered to avoid such violation. A corresponding
rule shall apply with respect to a failure to take an action that would adversely af fect the grandfather of the Pre-
409A Program. Any provision in this Plan
- 97 -

of the Pre-409A Program shall be void and without ef fect. In addition, any provision that is required to appear
in this Plan document to satisfy the requirements of Section 409A, but that is not expressly set forth, shall be
deemed to be set forth herein, and the Plan shall be administered in all respects as if such provision were
expressly set forth. A corresponding rule shall apply with respect to a provision that is required to preserve the
grandfather of the Pre-409A Program. In all cases, the provisions of this Section shall apply notwithstanding

summary:
- 409A compliance and grandfathering: Any Plan provision that violates Section 409A or harms the grandfathered Pre‑409A Program is void; any required 409A (or grandfathering) terms not expressly stated are deemed included and control over conflicting Plan terms.
- Transition Period rules for severance window programs: Detailed timing and form-of-payment rules for Participants who terminated in 2005, 2007, or 2008.
- Defined term: Special Early Retirement means age 50–54 with 10 years of Elapsed Time Service; for 2008 severance, age and service are rounded up to the nearest whole year when determining eligibility.
- 2005 severance:
  - Non‑retirement eligible: 409A Pension paid as a Vested Pension under Section 6.1(b), timed with the Salaried Plan benefit; if otherwise payable in 2007, pay at the later of January 1, 2007 or age 55. Forms per Section 6.2.
  - Retirement eligible as of Feb. 5, 2006: lump sum on the first day of the month after Separation from Service.
  - Retirement eligible due to additional credited service: lump sum on the first day of the month after Separation from Service.
  - Special Early Retirement eligible: lump sum on the first day of the month after Separation from Service.
- 2007 severance:
  - Non‑retirement eligible: Vested Pension under Section 6.1(b); forms per Section 6.2.
  - Retirement eligible at separation: lump sum on the first day of the month after separation, unless a valid Prior Payment Election under Section 6.1(a)(2) applies.
  - Become retirement eligible during paid leave: Vested Pension starting the first day of the month after the later of age 55 or separation; forms per Section 6.2. PEP Kicker (make‑whole for lost accruals) paid as a single lump sum on the same timing; subject to any Prior Payment Election.
  - Special Early Retirement eligible at separation: Vested Pension starting the first day of the month after age 55; forms per Section 6.2. PEP Kicker as lump sum after age 55; subject to any Prior Payment Election.
  - Become Special Early Retirement eligible during paid leave: same age‑55 timing and forms; PEP Kicker lump sum after age 55; subject to any Prior Payment Election.
- 2008 severance:
  - Non‑retirement eligible: Vested Pension under Section 6.1(b); forms per Section 6.2.
  - Retirement eligible at separation: lump sum on the first day of the month after separation; subject to any Prior Payment Election.
  - Become retirement eligible during paid leave: Vested Pension on the first day of the month after the later of age 55 or separation; forms per Section 6.2. PEP Kicker as lump sum on the same timing; subject to any Prior Payment Election.
  - Special Early Retirement eligible at separation or during paid leave: Vested Pension on the first day of the month after age 55; forms per Section 6.2. PEP Kicker as lump sum after age 55; subject to any Prior Payment Election.
- Key Employee delay: If the Participant is a “Key Employee,” any payment on account of Separation from Service is delayed per Section 6.6 (six‑month delay rule).
- Administrative/IRS compliance: Payments under this section were scheduled for the calendar year of termination as provided; Company elections complied with IRS Notice 2005‑1 and Section 409A (and Plan Section 19(c)).

- Scope: Transition rules within the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program applying to specific participant situations and to 409A Disability Pension pre-separation accruals.

- A.6 Certain Participants:
  - 2005 Band VI limited-duration assignments: Participants who terminated in 2005 while classified as Band VI (or equivalent) and served in limited-duration roles under five years are (i) deemed to have five years of PEP credited service and (ii) deemed vested under the Plan.
  - 2007 lump-sum election under Salaried Plan: For participants who, on October 9, 2007, elected a November 1, 2007 annuity start date with a single lump sum under the Salaried Plan, the portion of the Equalization Plan benefit not subject to Code Section 409A is paid as a single lump sum six months after the Salaried Plan annuity start date.
  - 2004 fixed payment date election: For participants who, on September 3, 2004, chose a February 1, 2005 fixed payment date, that date is the Plan benefit commencement date, and the benefit calculation includes service for consulting to be performed for the Company even if that consulting occurs after the payment date.

- A.7 Transition Rules for Article VI (409A Disability Pension—Pre-Separation Accruals):
  - Distribution timing and form: Payments of the portion representing pre-separation accruals begin March 1, 2009, using the same forms of payment available for a vested pension (with options differing for married vs. unmarried participants per Section 6.2).
  - Additional death benefit: If a participant receiving these pre-separation accrual payments dies before his expected mortality date (as defined by the Plan’s January 1, 2009 mortality table), the beneficiary receives a lump-sum actuarial equivalent of payments that would have been made from death to the expected mortality date, payable within 30 days of death. Participants may designate a beneficiary specifically for this additional benefit notwithstanding general Section 6.5 provisions.

title: Inclusion of Salary and Eligible Bonus:
heading: B.2 Inclusion of Salary and Eligible Bonus :
start_phrase: The Plan Administrator may specify that, pursuant to a Participant’ s participation in a severance window program provided by the Company , if a Participant receives a severance benefit pursuant to a Severance Program, all salary continuation and any Eligible Bonus that is payable during the first 12 months of a leave of absence period provided to the Participant under such Severance Program will be counted toward the Participant’ s Highest A verage Monthly Earnings, even if such salary or other earnings are to be received after a Participant’ s Separation from Service.
summary:
- Scope: Appendix B sets rules for how earnings and service are computed during certain severance windows under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.
- Key definitions:
  - Severance Program: A company program that pays severance while a participant is on a qualifying severance leave, recognized for Service and Credited Service under this appendix.
  - Eligible Bonus: An annual incentive under the Severance Program that counts toward Highest Average Monthly Earnings (HAME).
- Earnings treatment (B.2):
  - Salary continuation and Eligible Bonus payable during the first 12 months of a severance leave can be included in HAME, even if paid after Separation from Service.
  - If a 409A Pension is paid at Separation before all severance amounts are received, HAME is determined using the full projected salary continuation and Eligible Bonus for the first 12 months of leave.
  - The Plan Administrator will allocate projected earnings across Plan Years to avoid bunching.
- Credited Service treatment (B.3):
  - The first 12 months of severance can count as Credited Service for calculating the Participant’s Pension and any Pre-Retirement Spouse’s or Eligible Domestic Partner’s Pension, even if this period occurs after Separation from Service.
- Service treatment (B.4):
  - The first 12 months of severance can also count as Service for plan purposes (section continues beyond the excerpt).
- Administrative discretion:
  - In all cases, application of these inclusions is at the Plan Administrator’s discretion and may be specified in connection with a company severance window program.

B.2    Inclusion of Salary and Eligible Bonus :
The Plan Administrator may specify that, pursuant to a Participant’ s participation in a severance window
program provided by the Company , if a Participant receives a severance benefit pursuant to a Severance Program,
all salary continuation and any Eligible Bonus that is payable during the first 12 months of a leave of absence period
provided to the Participant under such Severance Program will be counted toward the Participant’ s Highest A verage
Monthly Earnings, even if such salary or other earnings are to be received after a Participant’ s

Service and prior to the Participant’ s receipt of all of the salary continuation or Eligible Bonus that is payable to the
Participant from the Severance Program, the Participant’ s Highest A verage Monthly Earnings shall be determined by
taking into account the full salary continuation and eligible bonus that is projected to be payable to the Participant

Administrator , in order to avoid any bunching of the earnings in a Plan Y ear.

title: Reduction to Reflect Early Payment:
heading: B.5 Reduction to Reflect Early Payment :
start_phrase: If the Participant receives either (1) additional Credited Service or (2) additional earnings that are included in Highest A verage Monthly Earnings under Sections B.2 or B.3 of this Article B, as a result of a severance benefit provided under a Severance Program and such additional Credited Service or earnings are included in the calculation of the Participant’ s Pension prior to the time that the Credited Service is actually performed by the Participant, or the earnings are actually paid to the Participant, the Pension paid to the Participant shall be adjusted actuarially to reflect the receipt of the portion of the Pension attributable to such Credited Service or earnings received on account of the Severance Program prior to the time such Credited Service is performed or such earnings are actually paid to the Participant.
summary: The excerpt clarifies that service credited under a severance program counts toward a participant’s pension and pre-retirement survivor benefits (spouse or eligible domestic partner) even if the credited period occurs after separation from service. It also establishes that if severance-related credited service or earnings (including amounts used in Highest Average Monthly Earnings) are included in the pension calculation before the service is performed or earnings are paid, the pension will be actuarially reduced to reflect early payment, using the early-payment rate from the Salaried Plan.

B.5    Reduction to Reflect Early Payment :
If the Participant receives either (1) additional Credited Service or (2) additional earnings that are included in
Highest A verage Monthly Earnings under Sections B.2 or B.3 of this Article B, as a result of a severance benefit
provided under a Severance Program and such additional Credited Service or earnings are included in the calculation
of the Participant’ s Pension prior to the time that the Credited Service is actually performed by the Participant, or the
earnings are actually paid to the Participant, the Pension paid to the Participant shall be adjusted actuarially to reflect
the receipt of the portion of the Pension attributable to such Credited Service or earnings received on account of the
Severance Program prior to the time such Credited Service is performed or such earnings are actually paid to the
Participant. For purposes of determining the adjustment to be made, the Plan shall use the rate provided under the
Salaried Plan for early payment of benefits.

summary:

- Eligibility:
  - Standard rule: Employee on assignment to an April 2007 Foreign Subsidiary in a Band 4 (or equivalent) or higher position.
  - Special rule for certain permanent assignments to Mexico: Individual would meet the Salaried Plan Employee definition (Section 2.1, Part B, para. (2)(vi) as of Jan 1, 2014) but for being in Band 4+; Mexico listed as home country with the Expat Centre for Excellence; and assignment not limited to 5 years or less.

- Defines “Year of Transfer” as the year in which a transfer described in subsection (f) occurs.
- Establishes the benefit formula for PIRP Transfer Participants, generally mirroring the methodology in Section 5.1 of the Plan, with special rules to coordinate benefits between the Salaried Plan and PIRP/PIRP-DB.
- Total Pension calculation:
  - First, compute as if the participant were an eligible employee under the Salaried Plan for the entire Year of Transfer, using actual Salaried Plan Credited Service and Earnings plus additional compensation/service that would have been recognized as PIRP-DB Salary/Pensionable Service if PIRP-DB Section 9.14 did not apply.
  - If PIRP-DB Salary or Pensionable Service in a year cannot be recognized because of PIRP-DB Section 9.14, the increase in the participant’s PIRP accrued benefit blocked by that section is added to the participant’s accrued benefit under this Plan. For separations on or after January 1, 2017, this results in a Company‑determined increase to Total Pension.
  - Prevents double counting and requires avoidance of duplicative benefits with PIRP-DB or other Company plans, while prohibiting any offset that would violate Code Section 409A.
- Benefit payable under this Plan:
  - Derived by applying the normal Article V reductions to the Total Pension.
  - For separations on or after January 1, 2017, if early retirement eligibility under PIRP-DB would have increased the PIRP-DB benefit but is blocked by Section 9.14, an appropriate Company‑determined increase is added to this Plan’s benefit (net of any early retirement increase already due under this Plan), again avoiding duplication and complying with Code Section 409A.
- Permits alternative arrangements: The Company and a participant who would qualify as an International Transfer Participant may, by written agreement, disregard this Article and adopt another benefit arrangement under the Plan that complies with Code Section 409A.

heading: E.1 Scope .
start_phrase: This Article E sets forth the time and form of payment provisions that apply to benefits under the Plan that are paid to a Covered Participant (as defined in Section E.2 below).
summary:
- Appendix Article E governs the time and form of payment of benefits made during severance windows under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.
- Scope: Applies to benefits paid to “Covered Participants” whose employment is terminated in a Severance Program or under an Individual Severance Agreement and who qualify for Special Early Retirement.
- Effective dates: Applies to terminations on or after January 1, 2009; for Participants covered by Appendix Article PBG, on or after January 1, 2012.
- Non-permanence: Clarifies that any additional benefits provided under Severance Programs or Individual Severance Agreements are not permanent features of the Plan.
- Definitions provided:
  - “Applicable Summary Plan Description” (SPD) is the SPD that sets the terms for a specific Severance Program.
  - “Covered Participant” is a Participant whose employment is terminated and who is eligible for Special Early Retirement either under a Severance Program per the Applicable SPD or under an Individual Severance Agreement.
- Interpretation: Capitalized terms not defined in Article E use the meanings from the main Plan unless context requires otherwise.

E.1    Scope .
This Article E sets forth the time and form of payment provisions that apply to benefits under the Plan that are
paid to a Covered Participant (as defined in Section E.2 below). This Article is ef fective for Participants who are
terminated in a Severance Program or under circumstances that qualify them for an Individual Severance Agreement
(each as defined in Section E.2 below) on or after January 1, 2009 (or in the case of Participants covered by
Appendix Article PBG, on or after January 1, 2012). Nothing in this Article E shall make any of the additional benefits
that are made available under the Plan in any Severance Program or pursuant to any Individual Severance
Agreement a permanent feature of the Plan.

title: Definitions:
heading: E.2 Definitions :
start_phrase: Where the following words and phrases appear in this Appendix E with initial capitals, they shall have the meaning set forth below unless a dif ferent meaning is plainly required by the context.
summary:
- Document scope: Appendix Article E of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program sets the time and form of payment rules for benefits paid during severance windows to certain terminated participants. It applies to terminations qualifying under a Severance Program or an Individual Severance Agreement on or after January 1, 2009 (or January 1, 2012 for those covered by Appendix Article PBG). It clarifies that any additional severance-related benefits are not permanent plan features.
- Key definitions:
  - Applicable Summary Plan Description: The SPD governing a specific Severance Program.
  - Covered Participant: A participant whose employment ends and who qualifies for Special Early Retirement via a Severance Program (per the applicable SPD) or an Individual Severance Agreement.
  - Individual Severance Agreement: A company-participant agreement detailing termination terms and either confirming Special Early Retirement eligibility under PEP or specifying pension benefits tied to the termination.
  - Kicker: The Special Early Retirement benefit equal to (early retirement benefit under the Salaried Plan and this Plan as of the Termination Date) minus (the vested pension under the Salaried Plan and this Plan as of the Termination Date). It is split into:
    - PEP Kicker: Replaces benefits that could have been earned under this Plan absent early separation.
    - Qualified Kicker: Replaces benefits that could have been earned under the Salaried Plan absent early separation.
    - Early retirement reduction factors for ages before 55 use the 56-to-55 monthly reduction rate unless a Severance Program uses a different factor in the Salaried Plan or an Individual Severance Agreement specifies otherwise.
  - Severance Program: As defined in Appendix Section ERW.2(f) of Part B of the Salaried Plan (legacy PepsiCo Appendix).
  - Special Early Retirement: Retirement meeting the SPD’s special early retirement conditions or expressly recognized in an Individual Severance Agreement.
  - Termination Date: The later of the Separation from Service or the projected end of any authorized severance leave under the applicable SPD or Individual Severance Agreement, determined using the formulas in effect when the legally binding right to special early retirement benefits arises (or as set by the Plan Administrator if special early retirement does not apply). Once set, it generally does not change after separation unless expressly provided.
- Payment rules for 409A Pension (excluding the Kicker for this section):
  - Non-retirement-eligible at Separation: Paid as a Vested Pension under Section 6.1(b), following the form-of-payment rules in Section 6.2.
  - Retirement-eligible at Separation: If eligible for Normal, Early, or Late Retirement under Article IV, paid as a Retirement Pension (details continue beyond the provided text).

E.2    Definitions :
Where the following words and phrases appear in this Appendix E with initial capitals, they shall have the
meaning set forth below unless a dif ferent meaning is plainly required by the context. Any terms used in this Article E
of the Appendix with initial capitals and not defined herein shall have the same meaning as in the main Plan, unless a
different meaning is plainly required by the context.
(a)    “ Applicable Summary Plan Description ” means the summary plan description that sets forth the
terms and conditions of a particular Severance Program.
(b)    “ Covered Participant ” means a Participant whose employment with the Company is terminated
and who is eligible for Special Early Retirement either (i) under a Severance Program and pursuant to the
terms of the Applicable Summary Plan Description, or (ii) pursuant to the terms of an Individual Severance
Agreement.

Participant that – (i) sets forth the terms and conditions of the Covered Participant’ s termination of employment
and (ii) expressly either (A) provides that the termination qualifies the Covered Participant for Special Early
Retirement under PEP , or (B) describes the pension benefits the Covered Participant will receive in connection
with the termination of employment.
(d)    “ Kicker ” means the Special Early Retirement benefit that is provided to a Covered Participant
pursuant to the terms of an Applicable Summary Plan Description or an Individual Severance Agreement and
that is equal to the following: (i) the Participant’ s benefit under the Salaried Plan and this Plan as of his
Termination Date, determined based on the benefit formulas and early retirement reduction factors for Early
Retirement Pensions under each plan, minus  (ii) the Participant’ s Vested Pension under the Salaried Plan and
this Plan as of the T ermination Date, determined based on the benefit formulas and reduction factors for
Vested Pensions under each plan. The Kicker shall be divided into the following components:
(1)    The “ PEP Kicker ,” which is the portion of the Kicker paid under the Plan as a replacement
for benefits that the Participant could have earned under the Plan but for his Separation from Service
(either in a Severance Program or pursuant to the terms of an Individual Severance Agreement) prior to
attaining Normal or Early Retirement under the Plan; and
(2)    The “ Qualified Kicker ,” which is the portion of the Kicker paid under the Plan as a
replacement for benefits that the Participant could have earned under the Salaried Plan but for his
termination of employment (either in

Normal or Early Retirement under the Salaried Plan.
In determining the early retirement reduction factors for ages before 55, the monthly rate of reduction
applicable between age 56 and age 55 shall apply unless (i) in the case of a Participant who is eligible for
Special Early Retirement under a Severance Program, a dif ferent factor is used in the Salaried Plan for
employees covered by the same Severance Program in which case such other factor shall be used, and (ii) in
the case of a Participant who is eligible for Special Early Retirement pursuant to the terms of an Individual

(e)    “ Severance Program ” has the same meaning that applies to that term under Appendix Section

(f)    “ Special Early Retirement ” means a retirement from the Company that either – (i) satisfies all of the

(g)    “ Termination Date ” means the later of – (i) the Covered Participant’ s Separation from Service, or
(ii) date as of which the Covered Participant’ s authorized severance leave of absence (if any) is projected to

Agreement, as

title: Time and Form of Payment for 409A Pension:
heading: E.3 Time and Form of Payment for 409A Pension :
start_phrase: If a Covered Participant is not eligible for Retirement as of his Separation from Service, the Participant’ s 409A Pension shall be paid as a V ested Pension under Section 6.1(b) according to the form of payment provisions applicable to V ested Pensions under Section 6.2.
summary:
- Establishes how a Participant’s Termination Date is determined when severance leave-of-absence formulas apply: it is set as of the Separation from Service date using formulas in the Applicable Summary Plan Description (SPD) or Individual Severance Agreement tied to special early retirement rights, or by the Plan Administrator if special early retirement doesn’t apply. Once set, the Termination Date does not change after Separation unless expressly provided in the SPD or Individual Severance Agreement.
- Defines timing and form of payment for a Covered Participant’s 409A Pension (calculated without the Kicker for this section):
  - Non-retirement eligible at Separation: paid as a Vested Pension under Section 6.1(b), with form of payment per Section 6.2.
  - Retirement eligible (Normal, Early, or Late) at Separation: paid as a Retirement Pension under Section 6.1(a)(1), or per a valid prior payment election under Section 6.1(a)(2) if one exists.
  - Becomes Normal/Early retirement eligible after Separation (including during paid leave of absence): paid as a Vested Pension under Section 6.1(b), form per Section 6.2.
  - Special Early Retirement eligible at Separation or becomes so during paid leave window: paid as a Vested Pension under Section 6.1(b), form per Section 6.2.
- Sets timing and form of payment for Kicker benefits:
  - PEP Kicker: paid as a single lump sum on the first day of the month following the later of the Participant’s 55th birthday or Separation from Service; a valid Prior Payment Election under Section 6.1(a)(2) controls even if the 409A Pension is paid as a Vested Pension under E.3(b)(2).
  - References both PEP Kicker and Qualified Kicker, though only the PEP Kicker payment details appear in the excerpt; a death-related provision begins but is truncated.
text:
E.3    Time and Form of Payment for 409A Pension :
A Covered Participant’ s 409A Pension (calculated without regard to the Kicker for purposes of this Section
E.3) shall be paid as follows:
(a)    Non-Retirement Eligible Participants : If a Covered Participant is not eligible for Retirement as of
his Separation from Service, the Participant’ s 409A Pension shall be paid as a V ested Pension under Section
6.1(b) according to the form of payment provisions applicable to V ested Pensions under Section 6.2.
(b)    Retirement Eligible Participants :
(1)    If the Covered Participant is eligible for a Normal, Early or Late Retirement Pension under
Article IV as of his Separation from Service, the Participant’ s 409A Pension shall be paid as a
Retirement Pension under Section
- 125 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Program6.1(a)(1); provided, however , that if the Participant made a valid prior payment election under Section
6.1(a)(2), his 409A Pension shall be paid as a Retirement Pension in accordance with such election.
(2)    If the Covered Participant becomes eligible for a Normal or Early Retirement Pension after
his Separation from Service, including during the period between his Separation from Service and the
last day of his paid leave of absence (if any), the Participant’ s 409A Pension shall be paid as a V ested
Pension under Section 6.1(b) according to the form of payment provisions applicable to V ested
Pensions under Section 6.2.
(c)    Special Early Retirement Eligible Participants : If a Covered Participant is eligible for Special Early
Retirement as of his Separation from Service or becomes so eligible during the period between his Separation
from Service and the last day of his paid leave of absence (if any), the Participant’ s 409A Pension shall be
paid as a V ested Pension under Section 6.1(b) according to the form of payment provisions applicable to
Vested Pensions under Section 6.2.

title: Time and Form of Payment of Kicker Benefits:
heading: E.4 Time and Form of Payment of Kicker Benefits :
start_phrase: A Participant’ s PEP Kicker shall be paid as a single lump sum on the first day of the month following the later of (i) the Participant’ s 55 birthday , or (ii) the Participant’ s Separation from Service; provided, however , that if the Participant made a valid Prior Payment Election under Section 6.1(a)(2), the Participant’ s PEP Kicker shall be paid according to such election (even in cases where the Participant’ s 409A Pension is paid according to Section E.3(b)(2) above).
summary:
- Defines how a Covered Participant’s 409A Pension is paid when retirement eligibility (Normal, Early, or Special Early) is reached after Separation from Service, including during any paid leave period:
  - If a valid prior payment election under Section 6.1(a)(2) exists, the 409A Pension is paid as a Retirement Pension per that election.
  - Otherwise, the 409A Pension is paid as a Vested Pension under Section 6.1(b), following the form-of-payment rules in Section 6.2.
  - Special Early Retirement eligibility at or after Separation also results in payment as a Vested Pension under Section 6.1(b) and Section 6.2.

- Sets timing and form of “Kicker” benefits:
  - PEP Kicker: Paid as a single lump sum on the first day of the month following the later of age 55 or Separation from Service; if a valid prior payment election under Section 6.1(a)(2) applies, it governs. If the participant dies after qualifying but before payment, it is paid in a single lump sum 60 days after death to the Surviving Spouse or Eligible Domestic Partner, or otherwise to the estate.
  - Qualified Kicker: Paid as a single lump sum on the first day of the month on or after the Termination Date, unless an Applicable Summary Plan Description or Individual Severance Agreement specifies a different time and/or form, in which case those terms control. Death benefits mirror the PEP Kicker rules.

- Requires a payment delay for “Key Employees” for any payments triggered by Separation from Service, in accordance with Section 6.6, unless an exemption from Section 409A applies.

E.4    Time and Form of Payment of Kicker Benefits :
A Covered Participant’ s PEP Kicker and Qualified Kicker shall be paid as follows:
(a)    PEP Kicker : A Participant’ s PEP Kicker shall be paid as a single lump sum on the first day of the
month following the later of (i) the Participant’ s 55  birthday , or (ii) the Participant’ s Separation from Service;
provided, however , that if the Participant made a valid Prior Payment Election under Section 6.1(a)(2), the
Participant’ s PEP Kicker shall be paid according to such election (even in cases where the Participant’ s 409A
Pension is paid according to Section E.3(b)(2) above). In the event the Participant diesth

Surviving Spouse or surviving Eligible Domestic Partner in a single lump sum 60 days following his death, and
if there is no Surviving Spouse or surviving Eligible Domestic Partner , then to the Participant’ s estate.
(b)    Qualified Kicker : A Participant’ s Qualified Kicker shall be paid based on his Separation from
Service as a single lump sum on the first day of the month coincident or next following his T ermination Date;
provided, however , that if the Applicable Summary Plan Description or Individual Severance Agreement that

Kicker but before it is paid, the Qualified Kicker shall be paid to his Surviving Spouse or surviving Eligible
Domestic Partner in a single lump sum 60 days following his death, and if there is no Surviving Spouse or
surviving Eligible Domestic Partner , then to the Participant’ s estate.

title: Delay for Key Employees:
heading: E.5 Delay for Key Employees :
start_phrase: Notwithstanding any provision of this Appendix E to the contrary , if a Participant is determined to be a Key Employee, any payment under this Article E that is made on account of his Separation from Service shall be subject to the required delay in payment for Key Employees under Section 6.6, except to the extent that the payment qualifies for an exemption from the application of Section 409A.
summary: The excerpt outlines payment rules under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan (409A Program) for “PEP Kicker” and “Qualified Kicker” benefits. If a participant dies after qualifying but before payment, both kickers are paid in a single lump sum 60 days after death to the surviving spouse or eligible domestic partner, or otherwise to the estate. The Qualified Kicker is generally paid as a lump sum on the first day of the month coincident with or following the participant’s termination date, unless an applicable summary plan description or individual severance agreement specifies a different time or form. Additionally, if the participant is a “Key Employee,” any payment triggered by separation from service is delayed per Section 6.6 to comply with Section 409A, unless an exemption applies.
text:
E.5    Delay for Key Employees :
Notwithstanding any provision of this Appendix E to the contrary , if a Participant is determined to be a Key
Employee, any payment under this Article E that is made on account of his Separation from Service shall be subject
to the required delay in payment for Key Employees under Section 6.6, except to the extent that the payment
qualifies for an exemption from the application of Section 409A.

title: Scope:

start_phrase: This Article applies to “Covered U.K. Employees” as defined in Section F .2 below .
summary:
- Establishes Appendix Article F of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program for U.K. participants who have U.S. service.
- Scope (F.1): Applies to “Covered U.K. Employees”; benefits are determined under Section F.3, then paid under the Plan’s standard time and form rules; all benefits are subject to Internal Revenue Code section 409A; the Article is restated effective January 1, 2016 (originally effective January 1, 2011 for pre‑2016 service).
- Definition (F.2): A “Covered U.K. Employee” is a participant in the PepsiCo U.K. Pension Plan who:

summary:
- Scope: Article F of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program addressing special pension equalization benefits for U.K. employees designated, at the Company’s sole discretion, as “Covered U.K. Employees” while they engage in U.S. Service.
- U.S. Service timing: Defines U.S. Commencement Date (first day subject to U.S. income tax) and U.S. Cessation Date (when no longer subject to U.S. income tax or, if earlier, when Article F benefits commence).
- Benefit formula: As of the Modified U.S. Cessation Date, the Article F benefit equals the Total U.K. Supplementary Benefit minus the Frozen U.K. Supplementary Benefit, both expressed as single lump sums payable at the Article F benefit commencement date.

- Valuation standards: Lump-sum values under Article F must be determined using actuarial assumptions that comply with the referenced section (aligned with Section 409A requirements).

title: Operating Rules:
heading: F.4 Operating Rules:
start_phrase: The following operating rules apply to the calculation in Section F .3. above.
summary:
- Defines “Frozen U.K. Supplementary Benefit” as the single-sum value of the participant’s benefit under the U.K. Supplementary Pension Appendix immediately before the U.S. Commencement Date, payable when Article F benefits begin, and calculated under Section F.4.
- Operating rules for calculating the Article F benefit:
  - Post–U.S. Cessation Date accruals in the PepsiCo U.K. Pension Plan generally do not reduce the Article F benefit; however, any excess offset that would have applied under the U.K. Supplementary Appendix can reduce the Article F benefit, to the extent compliant with IRC Section 409A.
  - Lump-sum values must use IRC Section 417(e) actuarial assumptions as applied under the Salaried Plan on the relevant determination date.
  - The Frozen U.K. Supplementary Benefit is determined assuming the employee voluntarily terminated all PepsiCo service immediately before the U.S. Commencement Date.
  - Mid-year amendments to the U.K. plans that would change the Section F.3 calculation are deferred to take effect prospectively the following year if needed to comply with Section 409A.
  - If an individual returns to U.S. service and again qualifies as a Covered U.K. Employee, Article F terms are reapplied; any new benefit is reduced by the lump-sum value of prior Article F benefits to prevent duplication.
  - If later covered by other plan provisions instead of Article F, any new benefit under those provisions is reduced by the prior Article F lump-sum value to avoid duplication.
- No Other Benefits: While classified (or but for specific clauses would be classified) as a Covered U.K. Employee, the individual is not entitled to other benefits under this Plan or the Salaried Plan; before all requirements are met to be a Covered U.K. Employee, there is no legally binding right to an Article F benefit, and the Company may in its discretion prevent entitlement (e.g., by not designating the individual).

start_phrase: A Covered U.K. Employee shall not be entitled to any other benefits under this Plan or the Salaried Plan while he is a Covered U.K. Employee (or while he would be a Covered U.K. Employee if clauses (iv) and (v) of Section F .2. were not included in the definition of Covered U.K. Employee).

- Coordination of benefits after status change: If a Covered U.K. Employee has already earned an Article F benefit, reaches their U.S. Cessation Date, and later returns to a role eligible under other plan provisions, the “Other Provisions” apply for the new service period, but any new benefit is offset by the lump-sum value of the prior Article F benefit to prevent double-counting.

title: Scope:
heading: I.1 Scope:
start_phrase: To ensure there will be no “material modification” of the Pre-409A Program, this Article provides a makeup benefit under the 409A Program that applies to certain participants in the Pre-409A Program (“Pre-409A Participants”) in lieu of updating the Pre-409A Program’ s actuarial factors for early commencement of Vested Pensions to be consistent with the “2019 Salaried Program Factors” (as that term is defined in the definition of Actuarial Equivalent).
summary:
- Establishes Appendix Article I of the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program to provide a “makeup” benefit for certain Pre‑409A Participants.
- Purpose: avoid a “material modification” of the Pre‑409A Program by not updating its early commencement actuarial factors; instead, a 409A Program makeup offsets early retirement reductions to align outcomes with the 2019 Salaried Program Factors.
- Application: 
  - If a participant is in both the Pre‑409A and 409A Programs, the makeup is provided under the main plan text.
  - If a participant is only in the Pre‑409A Program and otherwise not entitled to 409A benefits, this Article grants the makeup.
- Eligibility (as described in the excerpt):
  - Must be a Pre‑409A Participant receiving a Pre‑409A “Vested Pension” as an annuity starting before the Normal Retirement Date, on or after January 1, 2019.
  - The annuity must be reduced for early commencement under the Pre‑409A Program’s terms (further details continue beyond the excerpt).
text:
I.1    Scope:
To ensure there will be no “material modification” of the Pre-409A Program, this Article provides a
makeup benefit under the 409A Program that applies to certain participants in the Pre-409A Program (“Pre-
409A Participants”) in lieu of updating the Pre-409A Program’ s actuarial factors for early commencement of
Vested Pensions to be consistent with the “2019 Salaried Program Factors” (as that term is defined in the
definition of Actuarial Equivalent). In the case of participants in the Pre-409A Program who are also
Participants in the 409A Program (without regard to this Article), this makeup relating to the early
commencement reduction of V ested Pensions payable as annuities is provided under the main text of the
Plan. However , this makeup is provided under this Article in the case of af fected Pre-409A Participants who
are otherwise not entitled to a benefit under the 409A Program.

title: Eligibility Under This Article :
heading: I.2 Eligibility Under This Article :
start_phrase: To be eligible under this Article, an individual must be a Pre-409A Participant:
summary:
- Purpose and scope: Establishes a “makeup” benefit under the 409A Program to avoid materially modifying the Pre‑409A Program by not updating its early retirement actuarial factors. Instead, for certain Pre‑409A Participants, the plan provides a 409A makeup amount that aligns outcomes with the “2019 Salaried Program Factors.”
- Interaction with main plan: If a Pre‑409A Participant is also otherwise a participant in the 409A Program, the makeup is handled in the main plan text; this Article applies to affected Pre‑409A Participants who would not otherwise receive a 409A benefit.
- Eligibility criteria:
  - The individual is a Pre‑409A Participant receiving a Vested Pension annuity that starts before Normal Retirement Date but on or after January 1, 2019.
  - The early commencement reduction applied under the Pre‑409A Program is greater than it would be using the 2019 Salaried Program Factors.
  - The individual does not otherwise have a 409A Pension payable on or after January 1, 2019 (either because they are only entitled to a Pre‑409A Pension, or any 409A Pension began before January 1, 2019).
  - Such individuals are defined as “Eligible Persons.”
- Benefit amount and form:
  - Paid as a single lump sum.
  - Calculated as the Actuarial Equivalent of the difference between:
    1) The Single Life Annuity the person would receive if the 2019 Salaried Program Factors applied to their Pre‑409A Vested Pension (including any portion from the PEP Guarantee), and
    2) The Single Life Annuity actually payable under the Pre‑409A Program using its existing early commencement factors.
text:
I.2    Eligibility Under This Article :
To be eligible under this Article, an individual must be a Pre-409A Participant:
(a)    Who is paid a Pre-409A Pension that is (i) a “V ested Pension” under the Pre-409A Program, and
(ii) paid in the form of an annuity commencing as of a date prior to the Pre-409A Participant’ s Normal
Retirement Date but as of on or after January 1, 2019;
(b)     Whose Pre-409A Pension annuity under subsection (a) above is reduced for early
commencement under the terms of the Pre-409A Program by more
- 138 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Programthan it would be if the early commencement reduction were calculated using the 2019 Salaried Plan
Factors; and
(c)    Who otherwise would not have a 409A Pension that is payable ef fective as of January 1, 2019 or
later because, except as provided in this Article, the only PEP Pension to which the individual is entitled
is a Pre-409A Pension, or because his otherwise applicable 409A Pension commenced payment as of
prior to January 1, 2019.
An individual who satisfies all of the foregoing eligibility requirements shall be referred to as an “Eligible
Person” for purposes of this Article.

title: Benefit Amount Under This Article :
heading: I.3 Benefit Amount Under This Article :
start_phrase: The benefit amount for an Eligible Person under this Article shall be the single lump sum that is the Actuarial Equivalent of the dif ference between:
summary:
- Establishes who qualifies as an “Eligible Person” under the Article: individuals whose early commencement reduction under the Pre‑409A Program would be smaller if the 2019 Salaried Program early commencement factors applied, and who otherwise would not have a 409A Pension payable on or after January 1, 2019 because their only PEP Pension is a Pre‑409A Pension or their 409A Pension already began before January 1, 2019.
- Defines the benefit as a single lump sum equal to the actuarial equivalent of the difference between:
  - The Single Life Annuity the person would receive under the Pre‑409A Program if the 2019 Salaried Program early commencement factors applied (including any portion from the PEP Guarantee), and
  - The actual Single Life Annuity payable under the Pre‑409A Program using the then‑applicable early commencement factors (including any PEP Guarantee portion).
- Specifies the valuation timing: the lump sum is calculated as of the applicable commencement date; if that date is December 1, 2019 but the individual’s actual Pre‑409A Annuity Starting Date is earlier, the amount is determined at that earlier date and rolled forward with actuarial equivalent interest to December 1, 2019.
- Clarifies that only the new 2019 Salaried Program Factors effective January 1, 2019 are used—no alternative pre‑2019 factors.
- Sets payment timing: the lump sum is payable on the latest of (i) the first of the month following Separation from Service or (ii) December 1, 2019 (additional items may follow beyond the excerpt).
text:
I.3    Benefit Amount Under This Article :
The benefit amount for an Eligible Person under this Article shall be the single lump sum that is the
Actuarial Equivalent of the dif ference between:
(a)    The Single Life Annuity that would be payable to the Eligible Person under the Pre-409A Program
as of the Eligible Person’ s Annuity Starting Date under the Pre-409A Program if the 2019 Salaried
Program Factors for early commencement applied in calculating such Single Life Annuity (including with
respect to any portion of the Participant’ s Pre-409A Pension that is derived from the PEP Guarantee),
and
(b)    The Single Life Annuity that is actually applicable to the Eligible Person under the Pre-409A
Program as of the Eligible Person’ s Annuity Starting Date under the Pre-409A Program, because of the
early commencement factors that
- 139 -
PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Programare actually applicable in calculating such Single Life Annuity (including with respect to any portion of
the Participant’ s Pre-409A Pension that is derived from the PEP Guarantee).
Such Actuarial Equivalent lump sum shall be calculated as of the applicable commencement date specified in
Section I.4 below; however , if the applicable commencement date is the Section I.4(b) date ( i.e. December 1,
2019) and the Eligible Person’ s actual Annuity Starting Date under the Pre-409A Program precedes December
1, 2019, then the Actuarial Equivalent lump sum shall be determined as of such actual Annuity Starting Date
and then brought forward with Actuarial Equivalent interest to December 1, 2019. For purposes of subsection
(a) above, the 2019 Salaried Program Factors shall be solely the new factors applicable under the Salaried
Program as of January 1, 2019 (and no alternative calculation using the factors in ef fect before January 1,
2019 shall apply).

title: Time of Payment Under This Article :
heading: I.4 Time of Payment Under This Article :
start_phrase: The lump sum benefit calculated under this Appendix shall be payable as of the Eligible Person’ s applicable commencement date, which is the latest of the following:
summary:
- Defines how to calculate an Actuarial Equivalent lump-sum “make-up” benefit under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program for participants whose Pre-409A Pension annuities (with Annuity Starting Dates on or after January 1, 2019) were reduced using pre-2019 factors.
- Calculation rules: lump sum is based on the Single Life Annuity and includes any portion derived from the PEP Guarantee; it uses only the 2019 Salaried Program Factors (no pre-2019 alternatives). The valuation date is the applicable commencement date; if that date is December 1, 2019 but the participant’s actual Pre-409A Annuity Starting Date was earlier, the lump sum is first determined as of that earlier date and then brought forward with Actuarial Equivalent interest to December 1, 2019.
- Time of payment (I.4): the lump sum is payable as of the latest of (a) the first of the month after Separation from Service, (b) December 1, 2019, or (c) the first of the month after age 55 (with the age-55 rule not applying to benefits derived from Article PBG).
- If the commencement date is under (a), actual payment may be delayed per Plan section 6.6(a); interest is added for any delay per section 6.6(c).
- Non-duplication (I.5): the make-up benefit is reduced (but not below zero) to prevent any duplication where a participant’s 409A Pension already provides all or part of the same make-up (e.g., via early retirement reduction factors) or where the Plan Administrator determines duplication would otherwise occur; reductions are made at the Administrator’s discretion to eliminate overlap.
text:
I.4    Time of Payment Under This Article :
The lump sum benefit calculated under this Appendix shall be payable as of the Eligible Person’ s
applicable commencement date, which is the latest of the following:
(a)     The first of the month following the Eligible Person’ s Separation from Service,
(b)     December 1, 2019, or

PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Program(c)     The first of the month following the Eligible Person’ s attainment of age 55 (except that this
subsection (c) shall not apply to the extent that the Eligible Person’ s benefit is derived from Article PBG
of this Appendix).
In the event that the Eligible Person’ s applicable commencement date is the date in subsection (a) above, then
the date of actual payment of the benefit shall be delayed to the extent provided by Section 6.6(a) of the main

date shall be increased by interest for the period of delay as provided in Section 6.6(c) of the main text of the
Plan.

title: Non-Duplication of Benefits :
heading: I.5 Non-Duplication of Benefits :
start_phrase: The foregoing Sections of this Article are intended to provide a make-up benefit under the 409A Program for applying an early commencement reduction under the Pre-409A Program using factors that predate the 2019 Salaried Plan Factors, with respect to a Pre-409A Pension that is paid in the form of an annuity and that has an Annuity Starting Date of January 1, 2019 or later .
summary:
- Sets an alternative benefit commencement option: the first day of the month after the Eligible Person turns age 55, except for benefits derived from Article PBG.
- Provides that if the applicable commencement date is the one described in subsection (a), actual payment may be delayed under Plan Section 6.6(a), with interest added for the delay per Section 6.6(c).
- Establishes a Non-Duplication of Benefits rule: this Article is intended to provide a make-up benefit under the 409A Program to offset early commencement reductions applied under the Pre-409A Program using factors predating the 2019 Salaried Plan Factors, for Pre-409A Pensions paid as annuities with Annuity Starting Dates on or after January 1, 2019.
- Prohibits duplicative payments: if a participant’s 409A Pension already effectively provides some or all of the makeup (e.g., via early retirement reduction factors) or if granting the makeup would duplicate benefits, the Plan Administrator will reduce the makeup benefit (not below zero) to eliminate duplication; this rule overrides any conflicting plan provisions.
text:
I.5    Non-Duplication of Benefits :
The foregoing Sections of this Article are intended to provide a make-up benefit under the 409A Program for applying
an early commencement reduction under the Pre-409A Program using factors that predate the 2019 Salaried Plan
Factors, with respect to a Pre-409A Pension that is paid in the form of an annuity and that has an Annuity Starting
Date of January 1, 2019 or later . However , no duplication of benefits may occur at any time under the Plan.
Therefore, to the extent an Eligible Person has received or will receive a 409A Pension that, without regard to this
Article, ef fectively provides some or all of such makeup ( e.g., because the Eligible Person’ s 409A Pension was
reduced for early commencement using Early Retirement reduction factors), or to the extent that the Plan
Administrator concludes that providing the makeup under this Article would otherwise result in a duplication of
benefits, the makeup benefit under this Article shall be reduced (but not below zero) as the Plan Administrator deems
appropriate to eliminate all

PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan –409A Programduplication of benefits. This provision shall govern over any contrary provision of this Article or the Plan that might be
interpreted to support a duplication of benefits.

title: Scope :
heading: J.1 Scope :
start_phrase: This Article applies to “Covered International Employees” as defined in Section J.2 below .
summary:
- Appendix Article J covers special pension equalization provisions for “Certain International Employees Who Are U.S. Persons” under the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program.
- Scope (J.1): Applies to “Covered International Employees.” Their benefits are determined under Section J.3 and distributed under Section J.4.
- Definitions (J.2): A “Covered International Employee” is an employee of a Designated PepsiCo Affiliate who:
  - Is ineligible to participate in PERP,
  - Would be barred from earning a benefit under PIRP-DB by Section 9.14 of PIRP-DB due to U.S. Person status,
  - Is initially selected by the Vice President as eligible based on special circumstances affecting the employee’s ability to receive retirement benefits, and
  - Is subsequently determined by the Vice President to be entitled to Covered International Employee status.
- The Vice President has unfettered discretion over the initial selection and subsequent determination of Covered International Employee status.
text:
J.1    Scope :
This Article applies to “Covered International Employees” as defined in Section J.2 below . The benefit of a
Covered International Employee shall be determined as provided in Section J.3 below . A benefit determined for a
Covered International Employee under this Article shall be distributed as provided in Section J.4 below .

title: Definitions :
heading: J.2 Definitions :
start_phrase: Where the following words and phrases appear in this Article J with initial capital letters, they shall have the meaning set forth below , unless a dif ferent meaning is plainly required by the context:
summary:
- Purpose and scope: Article J governs pension treatment for certain international employees who are U.S. Persons, specifying eligibility, benefit determination, and (by reference) distribution rules.
- Eligibility and key definitions:
  - Covered International Employee: An employee of a non-U.S. Designated PepsiCo Affiliate who is ineligible for PERP, barred from PIRP-DB due to U.S. Person status, initially selected and then formally determined by the Vice President (in unfettered discretion) to be covered. No legally binding right to a benefit exists before the Vice President’s final determination, consistent with Code Sections 409A and 457A.
  - Designated PepsiCo Affiliate: A non-U.S. employing entity designated by the Vice President.
  - PERP and PIRP-DB are defined plan references; Selected International Employee is someone meeting initial criteria but not yet finally determined; U.S. Person status follows PIRP-DB; the Vice President is as defined under PIRP-DB.
- Benefit determination for Covered International Employees:
  - Calculated under the main Plan rules as if the employee were a Plan Participant, including distinctions between Vested vs. Retirement Pension, subject to modifications:
    - Apply benefit factors as if eligible for the Salaried Plan throughout relevant employment (subject to listed modifications).
    - Usual offsets under Section 5.1(a)(2) and (3) (Salaried Pension Plan and Pre-409A Plan) do not apply unless a specific “Reduction Amount” is listed in the Benefit Information Table; if listed, that amount is applied.
    - The PEP Guarantee (Section 5.2) does not apply.
    - If a “Service Start Date” is specified in the Benefit Information Table, it overrides actual service start for pension calculations.
- Distribution provisions are to be applied under Section J.4 (not included in the excerpt).
- Administrative notes: Final coverage determination is made in conjunction with the employee’s retirement and not before the year of the Section J.4 distribution date.

summary:

summary: Appendix Article K to the PepsiCo Pension Equalization Plan – 409A Program sets out the termination and liquidation of the portion of the 409A Program covering participants affected by the “Tiger Transaction,” effective upon the transaction’s Closing. It defines key terms, including Affected Participant (those experiencing the change in control due to the Closing), the Agreement (the August 2, 2021 Unit Purchase Agreement among PepsiCo, Bengal Beverages LP, Bengal Debt Merger Sub, LLC, and Naked Juice Co.), Closing, Related Amendments (other 409A arrangements treated as a single plan under Treas. Reg. §1.409A-3(c)(2)), and Tiger Transaction (a change in control under Treas. Reg. §1.409A-3(i)(5) for certain PepsiCo businesses). Each Affected Participant will receive a single lump-sum payment of their entire interest within 12 months of Closing, determined by treating the participant as having a Separation from Service at Closing and calculating the lump sum as of the selected distribution date within that 12-month period, all in full compliance with Section 409A regulations.
