- Plan Administrator (the Committee) has exclusive, absolute, and discretionary authority to interpret the Plan, determine eligibility and benefit amounts, and make all determinations; benefits are paid only if the Administrator decides the applicant is entitled. The Administrator may consider the Company’s intent in interpreting provisions. Decisions are final, conclusive, and reviewed by courts only under an arbitrary and capricious (abuse of discretion) standard.
- Compensation, indemnity, and liability: the Plan Administrator serves without bond and without compensation; all Plan and administrative expenses are paid by Employers and may, if deemed appropriate, be charged to specific Participant Accounts. Committee members and delegates are not liable for others’ acts or their own except for willful misconduct. Employers (other than the Company) will indemnify Committee members and certain delegates/employees for expenses and liabilities, including legal fees, arising from their service.
- Withholding and tax reporting: the Employer must withhold required federal, state, and local taxes from Plan amounts; collect/remit Social Security and Medicare taxes on deferred or accrued amounts; and report deferrals and taxable amounts on Form W-2 in accordance with Section 409A rules and procedures.

title: Section 16 Compliance
heading: 7.06 Section 16 Compliance:
start_phrase: In General . This Plan is intended to be a formula plan for purposes of Section 16 of the Act.
summary:
- Establishes Section 16 compliance by treating the plan as a “formula plan” intended to fit within Rule 16b-3, with administration by Compensation Committee delegates so initial Board Approval of the plan minimizes the need for transaction-specific approvals for Section 16 insiders.
- Defines “Covered Distributions” involving deferrals invested in the Phantom PepsiCo Common Stock Fund where payment timing could create a Section 16 opposite-way match. Sets rules that, if Board Approval hasn’t been obtained or if the liquidation is a discretionary transaction, the distribution will be delayed only until the earlier of: (1) Board Approval of the liquidation (for non-discretionary transactions), or (2) when making the distribution would no longer violate Section 16 (e.g., the participant is no longer a Section 16 insider, the subaccount is no longer invested in the phantom stock fund, or sufficient time has elapsed to avoid a match).
- Mandates conformance with Section 409A effective January 1, 2009, while preserving the grandfathered, exempt status of deferrals under the Pre-409A Program; this compliance section controls over any conflicting plan provisions.
text:
06    Section 16 Compliance:
        (a)    In General . This Plan is intended to be a formula plan for purposes of Section 16 of the Act. Accordingly , in the case of
a deferral or other action under the Plan that constitutes a transaction that could be covered by Rule 16b-3(d) or (e), if it were
approved by the Company’ s Board or Compensation Committee (“Board Approval”), it is intended that the Plan shall be
administered by delegates of the Compensation Committee, in the case of a Participant who is subject to Section 16 of the Act, in
a manner that will permit the Board Approval of the Plan to avoid any additional Board Approval of specific transactions to the
maximum possible extent.
        (b)    Approval of Distributions : This subsection shall govern the distribution of a deferral that (i) is wholly or partly
invested in the Phantom PepsiCo Common Stock Fund at the time the deferral would be valued to determine the amount of cash
to be distributed to a Participant, (ii) either was the subject of a Second Look Election or was not covered by an agreement, made
at the time of the Participant’ s original deferral election, that any investments in the Phantom PepsiCo Common Stock Fund
would, once made, remain in that fund until distribution of the deferral, (iii) is made to a Participant who is subject to Section 16
of the Act at the time the interest in the Phantom PepsiCo Common Stock Fund would be liquidated in connection with the
distribution, and (iv) if paid at the time the distribution would be made without regard to this subsection, could result in a
violation of Section 16 of the Act because there is an opposite way transaction that would be matched with the liquidation of the
Participant’ s interest in the PepsiCo Common Stock Fund (either as a “discretionary transaction,” within the meaning of Rule
16b-3(b)(1), or as a regular transaction, as applicable) (a “Covered Distribution”). In the case of a Covered Distribution, if the
liquidation of the Participant’ s interest in the Phantom PepsiCo Common Stock Fund in connection with the distribution has not
received Board Approval by the time the distribution would be made if it were not a Covered Distribution, or if it is a
discretionary transaction, then the actual distribution to the Participant shall be delayed only until the earlier of:
        (1)    In the case of a transaction that is not a discretionary transaction, Board Approval of the liquidation of the
Participant’ s interest in the Phantom PepsiCo Common Stock Fund in connection with the distribution, and
        (2)    The date the distribution would no longer violate Section 16 of the Act, e.g., when the Participant is no longer
subject to Section 16 of the Act, when the Deferral Subaccount related to the distribution is no longer invested in the
Phantom PepsiCo Common Stock Fund or when the time between the liquidation and an opposite way transaction is
sufficient.
7.

title: Conformance with Section 409A
heading: 7.07 Conformance with Section 409A:
start_phrase: Ef fective from and after January 1, 2009, at all times during each Plan Y ear, this Plan shall be operated (i) in accordance with the requirements of Section 409A, and (ii) to preserve the status of deferrals under the Pre-409A Program as being exempt from Section 409A, i.e., to preserve the grandfathered status of the Pre-409A Program.
summary:
- Section 16 compliance intent: The plan is designed as a “formula plan” under Section 16 of the Securities Exchange Act, administered by delegates of the Compensation Committee to allow broad Board Approval under Rule 16b‑3 to cover plan transactions and minimize the need for transaction‑specific approvals.
- Covered Distributions rules: For distributions involving amounts invested in the Phantom PepsiCo Common Stock Fund that could create a matchable opposite-way transaction for a Participant subject to Section 16 (including where a Second Look Election applies or investment wasn’t locked at the original deferral), the distribution is delayed if liquidation lacks Board Approval or if it is a discretionary transaction. Payment is deferred only until the earlier of:
  - Board Approval of the liquidation (for non‑discretionary transactions), or
  - The date the payment would no longer violate Section 16 (e.g., the Participant is no longer subject to Section 16, the subaccount is no longer invested in the phantom stock fund, or sufficient time has elapsed to avoid matching).
- Section 409A conformance: Effective January 1, 2009, the plan operates in full compliance with IRC Section 409A and preserves grandfathered, pre‑409A deferrals as exempt. This 409A conformity provision controls over any conflicting plan terms.

07    Conformance with Section 409A:
    Ef fective from and after January 1, 2009, at all times during each Plan Y ear, this Plan shall be operated (i) in accordance with

title: Claims for Benefits
heading: 8.01 Claims for Benefits:
start_phrase: The Plan Administrator has the discretionary right to modify the claims process described in this Section in any manner so long as the claims review process, as modified, includes the basic steps described in this Section and Section 8.02.
summary:
- Establishes Article VIII – Claims Procedure, outlining how to file and appeal benefit claims.
- Grants the Plan Administrator discretion to modify the claims process, provided the core steps in Sections 8.01 and 8.02 are maintained.
- Defines eligible “Claimants” broadly (participants, putative participants, beneficiaries, putative beneficiaries, and others).
- Requires claims to be submitted in writing (or another acceptable form) to the Plan Administrator.
- Initial claim determinations:
  - Denial notice due within 90 days of receipt, with one possible additional 90-day extension for special circumstances, with advance written notice stating reasons.
  - Denial notices must include the reasons, relevant Plan provisions, information needed to perfect the claim, and appeal procedures.
- Appeals of denied claims:
  - Claimant must file a written appeal within 60 days of receiving the denial.
  - Plan Administrator must provide a full and fair review, allowing submission of comments, documents, and records, considered even if not included initially.
  - Appeal decision due within 60 days, with one possible additional 60-day extension for special circumstances, with advance notice; in all cases, a decision no later than 120 days after receipt of the appeal.
  - Appeal decision notice must state the basis for the decision.
- COVID-19 deadline relief:
  - Notes DOL, Treasury, and IRS guidance effective March 1, 2020 through at least November 1, 2022, under ERISA §518 and Code §7508A(b), and EBSA Disaster Relief Notices 2020-01 and 2021-01.
  - Provides that up to one year may be disregarded for determining deadlines for plans, sponsors, administrators, participants, and beneficiaries due to the COVID-19 outbreak.
  - Plan will comply with these extensions as required; relief end-point language is introduced but truncated in the excerpt.
text:
01    Claims for Benefits:
    The Plan Administrator has the discretionary right to modify the claims process described in this Section in any manner so
long as the claims review process, as modified, includes the basic steps described in this Section and Section 8.02. If a
Participant, putative Participant, Beneficiary , putative Beneficiary or other person (hereafter , “Claimant”) does not receive timely
payment of any benefits which he or she believes are due and payable under the Plan, or if a Claimant believes some other right
derived from or related to the Plan has been withheld or abridged, he or she may make a claim for benefits to the Plan
Administrator . The claim for benefits must be in writing (or in such other form acceptable to the Plan Administrator) and
addressed to the Plan Administrator . If the claim for benefits is denied, the Plan Administrator will notify the Claimant within 90
days after the Plan Administrator initially received the benefit claim. However , if special circumstances require an extension of
time for processing the claim, the Plan Administrator will furnish notice of the extension to the Claimant prior to the termination
of the initial 90-day period (indicating the special circumstances that require the extension), and such extension may not exceed
one additional, consecutive 90-day period. Any notice of a denial of benefits shall advise the Claimant of the basis for the denial,
pertinent Plan provisions on which the denial is based, any additional material or information necessary for the Claimant to
perfect his or her claim, and the steps which the Claimant must take to appeal his or her claim for benefits.
8.

title: Appeals of Denied Claims
heading: 8.02 Appeals of Denied Claims:
start_phrase: Each Claimant whose claim for benefits has been denied may file a written appeal for a review of his or her claim by the Plan Administrator .
summary:
- Establishes the Plan Administrator’s discretion to modify the claims process, provided core steps in Sections 8.01 and 8.02 are preserved.
- Outlines initial claims process:
  - Claims must be submitted in writing (or another acceptable form) to the Plan Administrator.
  - Decision due within 90 days; may extend once for an additional 90 days with prior written notice stating special circumstances.
  - Denial notices must state the reasons, cite relevant Plan provisions, identify additional needed information, and explain appeal steps.
- Details appeal rights and procedures:
  - Claimant has 60 days from denial to file a written appeal.
  - Entitles Claimant to a full and fair review, including submitting comments, documents, and records, whether or not part of the initial determination.
  - Decision due within 60 days; may extend once for an additional 60 days with notice; in all cases no later than 120 days from appeal receipt. Decision notices must state the basis for the determination.
- Provides COVID-19 deadline relief:
  - Plan will follow DOL, Treasury, and IRS guidance permitting up to a one-year “disregarded period” for certain deadlines (including ERISA claims procedure deadlines and Plan notices/disclosures).
  - Relief ends on the earlier of one year from when relief first applied to the person or 60 days after the end of the National Emergency/Outbreak Period; no disregarded period exceeds one year; Outbreak Period ongoing as of November 1, 2022.
- Limits external review:
  - Any court, arbitrator, or tribunal review is limited to the administrative record before the Plan Administrator at the time of its determination.
  - Notices to claimants may be sent using methods permitted under DOL Reg. 2520.104b-1 or other applicable guidance.
- Sets special procedures for disability claims:
  - Disability-related claims and appeals follow DOL Reg. 2560.503-1 provisions specific to disability benefits (including cited subsections).
- Clarifies scope of discretion:
  - Specific references to the Plan Administrator’s discretion do not limit broader discretionary authority elsewhere in the Plan.
- Requires exhaustion of administrative remedies:
  - Claimants must fully exhaust the Plan’s claims procedures before filing in court or another tribunal.
  - Exhaustion is interpreted broadly; it is not excused for:
    - Failing to clearly submit a claim to the Plan Administrator, or
    - Failing to fulfill document requests unless strict conditions are met (ERISA requires the documents; written request addressed to and received by the Plan Administrator; failure to provide within six months or a reasonable longer period; and clear assertion of ERISA rights). Individuals not treated as Participants must clearly assert entitlement to Participant status.
  - Post-exhaustion litigation or review is, to the maximum extent permissible, limited to the administrative record.
text:
02    Appeals of Denied Claims:
    Each Claimant whose claim for benefits has been denied may file a written appeal for a review of his or her claim by the Plan
Administrator . The request for review must be filed by the Claimant within 60 days after he or she received the notice denying
his or her claim. Upon review , the Plan Administrator shall provide the claimant a full and fair review of the claim, including the
opportunity to submit to the Plan Administrator comments, document, records and other information relevant to the claim, and
the Plan Administrator ’s review shall take into account such comments, documents, records and information regardless of
whether it was submitted or considered at the initial determination. The decision of the Plan Administrator will be communicated
to the Claimant within 60 days after receipt of a request for appeal. The notice shall set forth the basis for the Plan
Administrator ’s decision. However , if special circumstances require an extension of time for processing the appeal, the Plan
Administrator will furnish notice of the extension to the Claimant prior to the termination of the initial 60-day period (indicating
the special circumstances that require the extension), and such extension may not exceed one additional, consecutive 60-day
period. In no event shall the Plan Administrator ’s decision be rendered later than 120 days after receipt of a request for appeal.
Effective March 1, 2020 and continuing at least through November 1, 2022, the Department of Labor , the Department of
the T reasury , and the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) (collectively the “Agencies”) extended certain deadlines applicable to the
Plan in light of the COVID-19 outbreak, pursuant to the authority granted in ERISA section 518 and Code section 7508A(b) and
as set forth in Disaster Relief Notices 2020-01 and 2021-01 issued by the Employee Benefits Security Administration (“EBSA”),
and the Notice of Extension of Certain T imeframes for Employee Benefit Plans, Participants, and Beneficiaries Af fected by the
COVID–19 Outbreak issued by the Agencies. The Plan will comply with these extensions as required by applicable law and
Agency guidance. Specifically , the Agencies provided that a period of up to one year may be disregarded in the case of an
employee benefit plan, sponsor , administrator , participant, beneficiary , or other person with respect to the employee benefit plan
in determining the date by which any action is required or permitted to be completed as a result of the Covid-19 outbreak. This
relief ends on the earlier of (a) 1 year from the date a person was
33first eligible for the relief, or (b) 60 days after the announced end of the National Emer gency (the end of the Outbreak Period),
which is still on-going as of November 1, 2022. In no case will a disregarded period exceed 1 year . This relief includes but is not
limited to notices and disclosures required by the Plan, and the deadlines under the ERISA claims procedure.
Any claim under the Plan that is reviewed by a court, arbitrator or any other tribunal shall be reviewed solely on the basis
of the record before the Plan Administrator at the time it made its determination. In addition, any such review shall be
conditioned on the Claimant’ s having fully exhausted all rights under this section as is more fully explained in Section 7.5. Any
notice or other notification that is required to be sent to a claimant under this section may be sent pursuant to any method
approved under Department of Labor Regulation Section 2520.104b-1 or other applicable guidance.

title: Special Claims Procedures for Disability Determinations
heading: 8.03 Special Claims Procedures for Disability Determinations:
start_phrase: Notwithstanding Sections 8.01 and 8.02, if the claim or appeal of the Claimant relates to Disability benefits, such claim or appeal shall be processed pursuant to the applicable provisions of Department of Labor Regulation Section 2560.503-1 relating to Disability benefits, including Sections 2560.503-1(d), 2560.503-1(f)(3), 2560.503-1(h)(4) and 2560.503-1(i)(3).
summary:
- Temporary deadline relief during the COVID-19 Outbreak Period: plan-related notices, disclosures, and ERISA claims procedure deadlines are tolled for the earlier of 1 year from when a person first became eligible for relief or 60 days after the National Emergency ends (still ongoing as of November 1, 2022). Notices may be delivered using DOL Reg. 2520.104b-1 methods.
- Any court, arbitration, or tribunal review of a claim is limited to the administrative record before the Plan Administrator at the time of decision and is conditioned on full exhaustion of plan remedies.
- Disability benefit claims and appeals follow the special procedures in DOL Reg. 2560.503-1, including subsections (d), (f)(3), (h)(4), and (i)(3).
- References to the Plan Administrator’s discretion do not limit the breadth of that discretion elsewhere in the Plan.
- Claimants must exhaust the Plan’s claims procedures before filing in court; the exhaustion requirement is to be interpreted as broadly as possible. Exhaustion is not excused unless strict conditions are met (e.g., clear, written ERISA document requests not fulfilled within a reasonable time, and clear indication of participant status or claim submission).
- After exhaustion, any judicial or tribunal review remains limited, to the maximum extent permissible, to the record before the Plan Administrator.
text:
03    Special Claims Procedures for Disability Determinations:
    Notwithstanding Sections 8.01 and 8.02, if the claim or appeal of the Claimant relates to Disability benefits, such claim or
appeal shall be processed pursuant to the applicable provisions of Department of Labor Regulation Section 2560.503-1 relating to

title: Effect of Specific References
heading: 8.04 Effect of Specific References:
start_phrase: Specific references in the Plan to the Plan Administrator ’s discretion shall create no inference that the Plan Administrator ’s discretion in any other respect, or in connection with any other provision, is less complete or broad.
summary:
- Temporary deadline relief tied to the COVID-19 National Emergency (Outbreak Period): certain plan notice/disclosure and ERISA claims-procedure deadlines are tolled, with any disregarded period capped at 1 year; Outbreak Period ongoing as of November 1, 2022.
- Court, arbitration, or tribunal review of claims is limited to the administrative record before the Plan Administrator at the time of its decision, contingent on the claimant’s full exhaustion of plan remedies.
- Claim-related notices may be delivered using methods approved under DOL Reg. 2520.104b-1.
- Disability benefit claims and appeals follow the special DOL Reg. 2560.503-1 procedures (including specified subsections).
- The Plan Administrator’s discretionary authority is broad; specific references do not limit discretion elsewhere in the plan.
- Mandatory exhaustion of the plan’s claims procedures before any lawsuit or tribunal action; the exhaustion requirement is to be interpreted as broadly as possible.
- Exhaustion is not excused unless the claimant clearly submitted a claim; document-request failures excuse exhaustion only if ERISA requires the documents, the written request was received by the Plan Administrator, the documents were not provided within 6 months (or a reasonable longer period), and the requester clearly asserted ERISA rights; non-participants must clearly claim entitlement to participant status.
- After exhaustion, any judicial or tribunal review remains limited, to the maximum extent permissible, to the existing administrative record.
text:
04    Effect of Specific References:
Specific references in the Plan to the Plan Administrator ’s discretion shall create no inference that the Plan
Administrator ’s discretion in any other respect, or in connection with any other provision, is less complete or broad.
8.

title: Claimant Must Exhaust the Plan’s Claims Procedures Before Filing in Court
heading: 8.05 Claimant Must Exhaust the Plan’s Claims Procedures Before Filing in Court:
start_phrase: Before filing any Claim (including a suit or other action) in court or in another tribunal, a Claimant must first fully exhaust all of the Claimant’ s rights under the claims procedures of this Article.
summary:
- Provides COVID-19 Outbreak Period relief for Plan deadlines and notices/disclosures: certain timeframes are tolled until the earlier of one year from when a person first became eligible for relief or 60 days after the National Emergency ends (still ongoing as of Nov. 1, 2022), with a maximum disregarded period of one year.
- States that any judicial, arbitral, or tribunal review of a Plan claim is limited to the administrative record before the Plan Administrator at the time of determination; notices to claimants may be sent using methods approved under DOL Reg. 2520.104b-1.
- Establishes special claims and appeals procedures for disability benefits in accordance with DOL Reg. 2560.503-1, including specified subsections.
- Clarifies that specific references to the Plan Administrator’s discretion do not limit the breadth of its overall discretionary authority.
- Imposes a strict exhaustion requirement: claimants must fully exhaust Plan claims procedures before filing in court or another forum; exhaustion is to be interpreted as broadly as possible and is a contractual precondition to any recovery related to the Plan.
- Details when exhaustion will not be excused, including standards for recognizing a claim submission and strict conditions for document requests (written, directed to and received by the Plan Administrator, ERISA-required, reasonable response period).
- Limits post-exhaustion judicial or tribunal review to the record considered in the claims procedure.
- Confirms exhaustion applies even if other, non-claim disputes are at issue, to rights provided in novel situations, to actual or potential rights, and even where specific procedures have not yet been defined (the Plan Administrator will establish or analogize procedures).
- Allows the Plan Administrator to make special arrangements for class-based consideration or to address conflicts to preserve the exhaustion requirement.
- Defines key terms:
  - Dispute: any claim, dispute, issue, assertion, action, or related matter.
  - Claim: disputes involving Plan interpretation, validity of adoption, administration, ERISA compliance, benefit recovery, fiduciary breach, or similar/related matters as determined by the Plan Administrator.
  - Claimant: employees, former employees, participants, beneficiaries, their spouses/former spouses, estates/heirs/representatives, and related individuals or groups asserting a Claim.
- Affirms the Plan’s intent to operate in good faith and consistently with ERISA, emphasizing uniform resolution of claims and avoidance of unnecessary litigation through comprehensive exhaustion.
text:
05    Claimant Must Exhaust the Plan’s Claims Procedures Before Filing in Court:
Before filing any Claim (including a suit or other action) in court or in another tribunal, a Claimant must first fully
exhaust all of the Claimant’ s rights under the claims procedures of this Article.
(a)    Upon review by any court or other tribunal, the exhaustion requirement of this Section 8.05 is intended to be
interpreted to require exhaustion in as many circumstances as possible (and any steps necessary to clarify or ef fect this intent may
be taken). For example, exhaustion may not be excused (i) for failure to respond to a Claim unless the purported claimant took
sufficient steps to make it reasonably clear to the Plan Administrator that the purported claimant was submitting a Claim with
respect to the Plan, or (ii) for failure to fulfill a request for documents unless (A) ERISA requires the documents to be provided in
response to the request, (B) the Claimant requests such documents in a writing that is addressed to and actually received by the
Plan Administrator , (C) the Plan Administrator fails to provide the requested documents within 6 months after the date the
request is received, or within such longer period as may be reasonable under the facts and circumstances, and (D) the requestor
took suf ficient steps to make it reasonably clear to the Plan Administrator that the requestor was asserting an ERISA right to the
documents. Accordingly , without limitation, a purported claimant or requestor who was not treated as a Participant shall not be
deemed to have taken suf ficient steps for purposes of the prior sentence unless he makes it reasonably clear to the Plan
Administrator that he is claiming to have been entitled to be a Participant.
(b)    In any action or consideration of a Claim in court or in another tribunal following exhaustion of the Plan’ s
claims procedure as described in this Section 8.05, the subsequent action or consideration shall be limited, to the maximum extent
permissible, to the record that was before Plan Administrator in the claims procedure.
34(c)    The exhaustion requirement of this Section 8.05 shall apply: (i) regardless of whether other Disputes that are
not Claims (including those that a court might consider at the same time) are of greater significance or relevance, (ii) to any rights
the Plan Administrator may choose to provide in connection with novel Disputes or in particular situations, (iii) regardless of
whether the rights are actual or potential and (iv) even if the Plan Administrator has not previously defined or established specific
claims procedures that directly apply to the submission and consideration of such Claim (in which case the Plan Administrator
(upon notice of the Claim) shall either promptly establish such claims procedures or shall apply (or act by analogy to) the claims
procedures of Section 8.05 that apply to claims for benefits).
(d)    The Plan Administrator may make special arrangements to consider a Claim on a class basis or to address
unusual conflicts concerns, and such minimum arrangements in these respects shall be made as are necessary to maximize the
extent to which exhaustion is required.
(e)    For purposes of this Section 8.05, the following definitions apply .
(1)    A “Dispute” is any claim, dispute, issue, assertion, action or other matter .
(2)    A “Claim” is any Dispute that implicates in whole or in part any one or more of the following –
(A)    The interpretation of the Plan;
(B)    The interpretation of any term or condition of the Plan;
(C)    The interpretation of the Plan (or any of its terms or conditions) in light of applicable law;
(D)    Whether the Plan or any term or condition under the Plan has been validly adopted or put into
effect;
(E)    The administration of the Plan;
(F)    Whether the Plan, in whole or in part, has violated any terms, conditions or requirements of
ERISA or other applicable law or regulation, regardless of whether such terms, conditions or requirements are, in
whole or in part, incorporated into the terms, conditions or requirements of the Plan;
(G)    A request for Plan benefits or an attempt to recover Plan benefits;
(H)    An assertion that any entity or individual has breached any fiduciary duty; or
(I)    Any Claim that: (i) is deemed similar to any of the foregoing by the Plan Administrator , or (ii)
relates to the Plan in any way .
It is the Plan Administrator ’s intent to interpret and operate the Plan in good faith and at all times consistently with any
applicable requirements of ERISA. Therefore, as a condition for any right or recovery related to the Plan, the Plan
imposes a contractual obligation for complete exhaustion under this Section with respect to any Claim (as defined above)
in order to allow for the ef ficient and uniform resolution of such Claims and to protect the Plan from potentially
substantial and unnecessary litigation expenses that exhaustion could obviate.
(3)    A “Claimant” is any actual or putative Employee, former Employee, Participant, former Participant,
Beneficiary (or the spouse, former spouse, estate, heir or representative of any of the foregoing individuals), or any other
individual, person, entity with a relationship to any of the foregoing individuals or the Plan, as well as any group of one or
more of the foregoing, who has a Claim.
358.

title: Limitations on Actions
heading: 8.06 Limitations on Actions:
start_phrase: Effective for claims and actions filed on or after April 1, 2016, any claim filed under Article VIII and any action filed in state or federal court by or on behalf of a former or current Employee, Participant, beneficiary or any other individual, person or entity (collectively , a “Petitioner”) for the alleged wrongful denial of Plan benefits or for the alleged interference with or violation of ERISA-protected rights must be brought within two years of the date the Petitioner ’s cause of action first accrues.
summary:
- Establishes a two-year statute of limitations (effective for filings on or after April 1, 2016) for any claim under Article VIII or court action by employees, participants, beneficiaries, or others alleging wrongful denial of plan benefits or interference with ERISA rights.
- Defines when a cause of action accrues:
  - For benefit claims: the earliest of (i) receipt of the benefits calculation at issue, (ii) the payment commencement date identified by the Plan Administrator, or (iii) when the petitioner has actual or constructive knowledge of the facts underlying the claim.
  - For interference with ERISA rights: when the claimant has actual or constructive knowledge of the alleged interfering acts.
- States that failing to file within the two-year period bars the petitioner and any representative from bringing the claim.
- Clarifies that correspondence or communications after completing the mandatory appeals process do not extend or affect the two-year limitations period.
- Imposes a venue restriction (effective for claims/actions filed on or after January 1, 2019): any court or tribunal action related to the Plan must be brought exclusively in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York.
text:
06    Limitations on Actions:
Effective for claims and actions filed on or after April 1, 2016, any claim filed under Article VIII and any action
filed in state or federal court by or on behalf of a former or current Employee, Participant, beneficiary or any other individual,
person or entity (collectively , a “Petitioner”) for the alleged wrongful denial of Plan benefits or for the alleged interference with
or violation of ERISA-protected rights must be brought within two years of the date the Petitioner ’s cause of action first accrues.
For purposes of this subsection, a cause of action with respect to a Petitioner ’s benefits under the Plan shall be deemed to accrue
not later than the earliest of (i) when the Petitioner has received the calculation of the benefits that are the subject of the claim or
legal action (ii) the date identified to the Petitioner by the Plan Administrator on which payments shall commence, or (iii) when
the Petitioner has actual or constructive knowledge of the facts that are the basis of his claim. For purposes of this subsection, a
cause of action with respect to the alleged interference with ERISA-protected rights shall be deemed to accrue when the claimant
has actual or constructive knowledge of the acts that are alleged to interfere with ERISA-protected rights. Failure to bring any
such claim or cause of action within this two-year time frame shall preclude a Petitioner , or any representative of the Petitioner ,
from filing the claim or cause of action. Correspondence or other communications following the mandatory appeals process
described in this Article shall have no ef fect on this two-year time frame.
8.

title: Restriction on Venue
heading: 8.07 Restriction on Venue:
start_phrase: Any claim or action filed in court or any other tribunal in connection with the Plan by or on behalf of a Petitioner (as defined in Section 8.06 above) shall only be brought or filed in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York, ef fective for claims or actions filed on or after January 1, 2019.
summary:
- Establishes a two-year statute of limitations for ERISA-related claims (wrongful denial of Plan benefits or interference with ERISA-protected rights) for claims/actions filed on or after April 1, 2016.
- Defines when a cause of action accrues:
  - Benefits claims: no later than the earliest of (i) receipt of the benefit calculation at issue, (ii) the payment commencement date identified by the Plan Administrator, or (iii) the Petitioner’s actual or constructive knowledge of the underlying facts.
  - Interference claims: when the claimant has actual or constructive knowledge of the alleged interfering acts.
- Failure to file within two years bars the Petitioner or any representative from bringing the claim; communications after the mandatory appeals process do not extend or affect the two-year period.
- “Petitioner” includes former/current employees, participants, beneficiaries, and any other individual, person, or entity acting on their behalf.
- Sets exclusive venue for litigation: all Plan-related court or tribunal actions by or on behalf of a Petitioner must be filed only in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, effective for filings on or after January 1, 2019.

title: Termination of Plan
heading: 9.02 Termination of Plan:
start_phrase: (a) The Company expects to continue this Plan, but does not obligate itself to do so.
summary:
- Amendment of the Plan (Article IX, 9.01):
  - The Compensation Committee (or its delegates) may amend the Plan at any time and in any manner, including deferral election methods and distribution terms/form/timing.
  - No amendment may reduce amounts already credited to a Participant’s Account, except for clarifying changes to avoid inappropriate windfalls.
  - As of September 25, 2019, the Company’s EVP and Chief Human Resources Officer (or functional successor) is delegated authority to amend the Plan, except for matters subject to Section 7.06.
  - Amendments must be in writing and adopted by the Committee or its delegates; all Participants and Beneficiaries are bound.
  - All amendments must comply with Section 409A.

- Termination of the Plan (Article IX, 9.02):
  - The Company may terminate or partially terminate the Plan at any time via the Compensation Committee or the full Board, including in response to tax law changes.
  - Termination cannot reduce amounts already credited to Participant Accounts; the termination resolution will specify distribution methods for credited amounts.
  - Termination and any related distributions must comply with Section 409A.
  - The Company retains maximum discretionary authority, to the extent permitted by Section 409A, to terminate and make distributions in connection with a Change in Control (as defined in Section 409A); these are the exclusive terms for change-in-control distributions under this 409A program.

- Limitation on Participant Rights (Article X, 10.01):
  - Participation does not guarantee continued employment or confer rights in employer assets beyond Plan provisions.
  - Employers may terminate employment without liability under the Plan, other than paying deferrals as provided.

- Unfunded Status and Employer Liability (Article X, 10.02):
  - The Plan is unfunded; benefits are paid from the general assets of the Participant’s individual Employer.
  - Participants and Beneficiaries have no property interest in specific assets and are general unsecured creditors of the individual Employer; no other Employer guarantees or shares the obligation.
  - Upon transfer between Employers within the organization, liability for prior deferrals shifts to the new Employer; if transferring outside the PepsiCo Organization, liability remains with the last PepsiCo Employer.
  - For this section, “Employer” refers only to entities within the PepsiCo Organization.

- Coordination with Other Plans (Article X, 10.03):
  - The Plan does not affect eligibility for or benefits under other employer benefit plans unless those plans state otherwise or to prevent jeopardizing favorable tax status.

- Receipt and Release (Article X, 10.04):
  - Payments made under the Plan satisfy claims to the extent paid; the Plan Administrator may require a signed receipt and release as a condition of payment.

- Governing Law (Article X, 10.05):
  - The Plan is governed by applicable federal law and, where not preempted, by other applicable law (state law reference incomplete in excerpt).

summary:

- Coordination with other plans: Rights to participate in other benefit plans are unaffected unless those plans state otherwise or compliance/tax-favored status would be compromised.
- Receipt and release: Payments to a participant satisfy claims against the plan administrator, recordkeeper, company, and employers to that extent; administrator may require a signed receipt/release as a condition of payment.

Participants and beneficiaries have no property interest in specific assets and are general unsecured creditors. No employer guarantees another’s obligations. Liability transfers between employers within the PepsiCo Organization upon an internal transfer; if a participant moves to a non-PepsiCo entity, liability for prior deferrals stays with the last PepsiCo employer.

text:
02    Unfunded Obligation of Individual Employer:
    (a)    The benefits provided by this Plan are unfunded. All amounts payable under this Plan to Participants are paid from
the general assets of the Participant’ s individual Employer . Nothing contained in this Plan requires an Employer to set aside or
hold in trust any amounts or assets for the purpose of paying benefits to Participants. Neither a Participant, Beneficiary , nor any
other person shall have any property interest, legal or equitable, in any specific Employer asset. This Plan creates only a
contractual obligation on the part of a Participant’ s individual Employer , and the Participant has the status of a general unsecured
creditor of this Employer with respect to amounts of compensation deferred hereunder . Such a Participant shall not have any
preference or priority over the rights of any other unsecured general creditor of the Employer . No other Employer guarantees or
shares such obligation, and no other Employer shall have any liability to the Participant or his or her Beneficiary . In the event a
Participant transfers from the employment of one Employer to another , the former Employer shall transfer the liability for
deferrals made while the Participant was employed by that Employer to the new Employer (and the books of both Employers
shall be adjusted appropriately).
    (b)    Notwithstanding the provisions of Subsection (a), for purposes of this Section an “Employer” shall only refer to
those entities which are part of the PepsiCo Or ganization. If a Participant transfers to an entity that is not part of the PepsiCo
Organization, the liability for deferrals made while the Participant was employed by the PepsiCo Or ganization shall remain with
his or her last Employer that was part of the PepsiCo Or ganization.

summary:
- Confirms participation does not guarantee continued employment or any property interest in employer assets; employer may terminate employment without plan liability beyond owed deferrals.

title: Adoption of Plan by Related Employers
heading: 10.06 Adoption of Plan by Related Employers:
start_phrase: The Plan Administrator may select as an Employer (other than the Company , which is automatically an Employer hereunder) any division of the Company , as well as any subsidiary or af filiate related to the Company by ownership (and that is a member of the PepsiCo Or ganization), and permit or cause such division, subsidiary or af filiate to adopt the Plan.
summary:
- Governing law and severability: The plan is governed by New York law, and if any provision is deemed invalid, the remainder stays effective.
- Adoption by related employers: The Plan Administrator may allow divisions, subsidiaries, or affiliates within the PepsiCo Organization to adopt the plan, with the effective date and adoption requirements at the Administrator’s sole discretion; determinations are final and conclusive.
- Interpretation rules: Singular/plural and gendered terms are interchangeable; “including” is to be read as “including without limitation,” and examples do not limit scope.
- Successors and nonalienation: The plan binds parties and their successors, but participants’ account amounts cannot be assigned, transferred, pledged, or garnished (including in divorce/child support), except that the Administrator may make payments pursuant to court orders as cash is paid from a participant’s Deferral Subaccount, reducing the participant’s account.
- Facility of payment: If a participant or beneficiary is legally disabled or incapacitated, the Administrator may direct payment to the person, their legal representative, or for their benefit; such payment fully discharges the plan’s liability.

summary:

- Sets eligibility rules:
  - Individuals hired by a PepsiCo Business after the Effective Time are eligible under the Plan upon meeting standard eligibility (and not eligible for another PepsiCo Organization nonqualified DC plan), unless they were employed immediately beforehand by a non-PepsiCo Business within the organization.
  - PAS/PBG Executives are generally ineligible, except that those hired by a PAS or PBG Business on/after the Effective Time who were Executives immediately before that hire may continue participating so long as they remain continuously employed within the PepsiCo Organization, as if they had remained Executives.
  - PAS/PBG Executives may defer Bonus Compensation beginning with the Plan Year starting January 1, 2010, and Base Compensation beginning with the Plan Year starting January 1, 2011, subject to the Plan’s main terms.

- Defines eligibility and participation rules for PAS Executives and PBG Executives under a PepsiCo deferred compensation Plan.
- Individuals hired by a PepsiCo Business after the Effective Time may participate once eligibility requirements are met and generally may not participate in another PepsiCo entity’s nonqualified defined contribution plan, unless they were immediately prior employed by a PepsiCo Organization member that is not a PepsiCo Business.
- PAS and PBG Executives are generally ineligible to participate; exception: an individual hired by a PAS or PBG Business on/after the Effective Time who was an Executive immediately before that hire may continue participating for as long as continuously employed within the PepsiCo Organization, as if still an Executive.
- Deferral timing for PAS and PBG Executives: eligible to defer Bonus Compensation beginning with the performance period for the Plan Year starting January 1, 2010, and Base Compensation beginning with the Plan Year starting January 1, 2011.

C.1    Scope .

title: Scope
heading: C.1 Scope .
start_phrase: This Article C provides for the termination and liquidation, in accordance with T reasury Regulation § 1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B), of the portion of the 409A Program that relates to certain Participants who are af fected by the “Closing” of the “T ransaction” (as those terms are defined below).
summary:
- Purpose and scope: Terminates and liquidates the portion of the 409A Program covering participants affected by a change in control resulting from the Transaction’s Closing, in compliance with Treasury Regulation §1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B). Article C is effective as of the Closing.

- Key definitions:
  - Affected Participant: Any participant who experiences the change in control due to the Closing, as defined under §1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B).
  - Agreement: Unit Purchase Agreement dated August 2, 2021 among PepsiCo, Inc., Bengal Beverages LP, Bengal Debt Merger Sub, LLC, and Naked Juice Co.
  - Closing: Consummation of the Transaction per Section 2.3 of the Agreement.
  - Transaction: The transactions under the Agreement that cause a change in control under §1.409A-3(i)(5) for certain PepsiCo businesses.

- Termination mechanics:
  - The 409A Program is intended to be irrevocably terminated for Affected Participants effective January 18, 2023 (12 months after the Closing).
  - The plan sponsor may revoke this termination through January 17, 2023; absent timely revocation, the termination becomes irrevocable on January 18, 2023 pursuant to §1.409A-3.

- Distribution mechanics:
  - Upon irrevocable termination, each Affected Participant will receive a single lump-sum payment of their entire unpaid 409A Program interest on January 1, 2024, and in any event no later than January 17, 2024, in full conformity with §1.409A-3(j)(4)(ix)(B).
  - The lump sum includes all remaining installments or other future-dated distributions.
  - Amounts are valued using the Program’s standard lump-sum valuation rules in effect on January 1, 2024.

start_phrase: We consent to the incorporation by reference in the registration statements and Forms listed below of PepsiCo, Inc. and subsidiaries (PepsiC o, Inc.) of our report dated February 8, 2023, with respect to the Consolidated Balance Sheet of PepsiCo, Inc. as of December 31, 2022 and December 25, 2021, and the related Consolidated Statements of Income, Comprehensive Income, Cash Flows, and Equity for each of the fiscal years in the three-year period ended December 31, 2022, and the related notes (collectively , the consolidated financial statements), and the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2022, which report appears in the December 31, 2022 annual report on Form 10-K of PepsiCo, Inc.
summary:
- Auditor consent: KPMG LLP consents to the incorporation by reference of its February 8, 2023 audit report on PepsiCo, Inc.’s consolidated financial statements for the three years ended December 31, 2022 and on the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2022, as included in PepsiCo’s 2022 Form 10-K.
- Scope of incorporation: Consent applies to multiple PepsiCo registration statements, including numerous Form S-3 automatic shelf registration statements and a wide range of Form S-8 filings for employee benefit and incentive plans (e.g., PepsiCo Savings Plans, SharePower Stock Option Plan, Director Stock Plan, various 401(k) and long-term incentive plans for PepsiCo, Quaker, Tropicana, PBG, and PepsiAmericas), with specific registration numbers listed.
- Execution details: Consent signed by KPMG LLP in New York, New York, dated February 8, 2023.
- Exhibit 24 – Power of Attorney: PepsiCo and certain officers/directors appoint David Flavell, Cynthia A. Nastanski, and Heather A. Hammond as attorneys-in-fact, each with authority to execute and file specified SEC registration statements and any necessary amendments (including post-effective amendments).
- Covered filings under the Power of Attorney: Enumerated S-3 automatic shelves for offerings of common stock, debt securities, warrants, units, and guarantees; registration statements for debt/warrants/guarantees; acquisition-related common stock registrations; and S-8 registrations tied to various stock option, long-term incentive, savings, and 401(k) plans, with detailed registration numbers provided.

title: CERTIFICATION
heading: EXHIBIT 31 CERTIFICATION
start_phrase: 1.I have reviewed this annual report on Form 10-K of PepsiCo, Inc.;
summary:
- Exhibit 31 CEO certification for PepsiCo’s Form 10-K, signed by Chairman and CEO Ramon L. Laguarta on February 8, 2023.
- Affirms the CEO reviewed the 10-K and that it contains no material misstatements or omissions.
- States the financial statements and other financial information fairly present, in all material respects, the company’s financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows for the periods presented.
- Confirms responsibility, with the other certifying officer, for establishing and maintaining disclosure controls and procedures and internal control over financial reporting.
- Asserts that such controls were designed (or overseen in their design) to ensure material information is communicated appropriately and to provide reasonable assurance on reliable financial reporting in accordance with GAAP.
- Reports that the effectiveness of disclosure controls and procedures was evaluated, with conclusions presented in the report as of period-end.
- Discloses whether any changes in internal control over financial reporting occurred during the most recent fiscal quarter that materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, those controls.
- Confirms disclosure to auditors and the audit committee of all significant deficiencies and material weaknesses in internal control over financial reporting, and of any fraud (material or not) involving management or employees with significant roles in internal controls.
text:
EXHIBIT 31
CERTIFICATION
I, Ramon L. Laguarta, certify that:
 
1.I have reviewed this annual report on Form 10-K of PepsiCo, Inc.;
2.Based on my knowledge, this report does not contain any untrue statement of a material fact or omit to state a material fact necessary to
make the statements made, in light of the circumstances under which such statements were made, not misleading with respect to the
period covered by this report;
3.Based on my knowledge, the financial statements, and other financial information included in this report, fairly present in all material
respects the financial condition, results of operations and cash flows of the registrant as of, and for, the periods presented in this report;
4.The registrant’s other certifying officer and I are responsible for establishing and maintaining disclosure controls and procedures (as
defined in Exchange Act Rules 13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e)) and internal control over financial reporting (as defined in Exchange Act Rules
13a-15(f) and 15d-15(f)) for the registrant and have:
a)Designed such disclosure controls and procedures, or caused such disclosure controls and procedures to be designed under our
supervision, to ensure that material information relating to the registrant, including its consolidated subsidiaries, is made known to us
by others within those entities, particularly during the period in which this report is being prepared;
b)Designed such internal control over financial reporting, or caused such internal control over financial reporting to be designed under
our supervision, to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial
statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles;
c)Evaluated the effectiveness of the registrant’s disclosure controls and procedures and presented in this report our conclusions about
the effectiveness of the disclosure controls and procedures, as of the end of the period covered by this report based on such
evaluation; and
d)Disclosed in this report any change in the registrant’s internal control over financial reporting that occurred during the registrant’s
most recent fiscal quarter (the registrant’s fourth fiscal quarter in the case of an annual report) that has materially affected, or is
reasonably likely to materially affect, the registrant’s internal control over financial reporting; and
5.The registrant’s other certifying officer and I have disclosed, based on our most recent evaluation of internal control over financial
reporting, to the registrant’s auditors and the audit committee of the registrant’s board of directors (or persons performing the equivalent
functions):
a)All significant deficiencies and material weaknesses in the design or operation of internal control over financial reporting which are
reasonably likely to adversely affect the registrant’s ability to record, process, summarize and report financial information; and
b)Any fraud, whether or not material, that involves management or other employees who have a significant role in the registrant’s
internal control over financial reporting.
Date: February 8, 2023   /s/ Ramon L. Laguarta

Chairman of the Board of Directors and
